💡 Key Takeaways

  • Top Wall Street analysts' recommendations can help investors gain clarity, as these experts conduct in-depth research to pick stocks with attractive growth prospects.
  • Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that investors have been grappling with stock market volatility, weighing elevated oil prices, persistent geopolitical tensions, the Federal Reserve's rate hike and a debate about AI safety. For all that, it helps to look beyond short-term noise and focus on stocks with strong long-term growth potential.

Top Wall Street analysts' recommendations can help investors gain clarity, as these experts conduct in-depth research to pick stocks with attractive growth prospects.

Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Recent findings suggest that enterprise software and cloud infrastructure firm Oracle (ORCL) recently unveiled better-than-expected results for the first quarter of fiscal 2027. The quarter benefited from solid growth in cloud infrastructure revenue.

After hosting a series of investor meetings with Ken Bond, Oracle head of investor relations following Q1 earnings, Guggenheim analyst John DiFucci reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $400. Oracle remains a Guggenheim Best Idea, he mentioned.

According to recent reports, "We continue to believe ORCL is a decade stock, driven by the massive (and profitable) opportunity ahead for AI training and inferencing," remarked DiFucci. He also cited the traditional Public Cloud business and additional AI-enabled cloud database and cloud applications for his bullish stance. DiFucci expects all the factors to drive revenue and profit acceleration over the next few years.

While Oracle delivered 850 MW of data center capacity in Q1 FY27, Bond cautioned that Infrastructure as a Service revenue in any quarter depends more on the timing of when that capacity comes online, than on the headline MW number. DiFucci expects IaaS growth to stay strong, with full-year growth expected above Q1 FY27's 120% constant currency rate. Management expects total revenue growth to accelerate sequentially throughout fiscal 2027, as the faster-growing infrastructure business makes up a larger share of the mix.

DiFucci addressed concerns regarding customer concentration, saying OpenAI's share of total remaining performance obligations has dropped from 80% last June to about 50% now, and is expected to keep falling as new contracts are signed with new and existing customers.

DiFucci ranks No. 263 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 62% of the time, delivering an average return of about 17.5%. See Oracle Insider Trading Activity on TipRanks.

Space systems and launch services provider Rocket Lab (RKLB) was recently initiated as a buy with an $80 price target by Raymond James analyst Brian Gesuale.

"RKLB has assembled launch, spacecraft, components, payloads and optical communications, with Neutron and Iridium completing medium-lift and applications/spectrum in 2027," said Gesuale.

The 5-star analyst highlighted that with the completion of the Iridium acquisition, Rocket Lab will become the only vertically integrated space tech giant with positive free cash flow (FCF). The deal will add a deployed constellation valued at more than $3 billion, globally coordinated L-band spectrum and about $500 million in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) and $300 million in free cash flow (FCF).

In a recent development, gesuale highlighted RKLB's strong revenue and backlog growth and progress toward positive EBITDA and FCF in 2027/2028. Rocket Lab is moving from a heavy investment phase into monetization, with estimated revenue growth of 59% in 2026, the analyst said, noting that RKLB's backlog has more than doubled to almost $2.4 billion from $1.1 billion in Q3 2025.

Given strong growth projections, the analyst expects RKLB's gross margins to expand from about a 35% trough in 2027 to about 47% by 2030, while R&D spending is estimated to decline from ~35% of sales in 2026 to about 10% in 2028, creating substantial operating leverage as the platform matures.

Sources indicate that gesuale ranks No. 369 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of about 17%. See Rocket Lab Statistics on TipRanks.

Recent findings suggest that J.P. Morgan analyst Doug Anmuth recently upgraded Meta Platforms (META) to buy from hold and raised his price target to $820 from $640. Despite the year-to-date underperformance of META, the 5-star analyst still sees significant upside, as Meta is in the early stages of launching frontier models and AI-powered offerings beyond advertising, particularly the Muse AI agent and Meta Model API access.

"Frontier models are at the core of Meta's product and monetization pipeline over a multi-year period, and its path toward superintelligence," noted Anmuth.

In the summer of 2025, Meta set a goal to rebuild its Meta Superintelligence Labs team and deliver frontier AI models within a year, the analyst noted. The team appears to have met its goal, rapidly advancing from the rollout of Muse Spark 1.1 in July to Muse Spark 1.3, which is competitive with Claude and GPT models, Anmuth said.

In a recent development, meanwhile, Meta's Watermelon product will expand opportunities in consumer products, business intelligence, and Family of Apps engagement, the analyst said. The product will enhance internal operations and overall efficiency, said Anmuth, who's confident of Meta's ability to bring consumer-driven AI products to its extensive user base of 4 billion and views its distribution network as a competitive advantage.

While Meta has focused on frontier models and AI product development, Anmuth also sees solid opportunity in its AI infrastructure capacity, which he believes will support future compute needs.

In a recent development, anmuth ranks No. 832 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 57% of the time, delivering an average return of about 9.40%. See Meta Platforms Financials on TipRanks.

So if you look at Bitcoin mining at a $65,000 Bitcoin price and using a very common air-cooled latest gen Bitmain Antminer S21 XP, that yields about $94 a megawatt hour. And then when we compare this to AI and HPC co-location hosting revenues, we're looking at about $220 a megawatt hour. Recent findings suggest that anthropic's IPO is coming this week, with the tech stock expected to trade by Thursday under the ticker symbol ANT. Its valuation will be high, projected to be around $1.4 trillion in market cap, but that's not nearly as high as it was expected to be previously, when analysts thought it could fetch close to $2 trillion, which would eclipse the roughly $1.8 trillion valuation at which Space Exploration Technologies Corp (SPCX +0.17%) went public earlier this year.

Even though it won't be a record-breaking IPO, Anthropic will be among the most valuable companies in the world when it goes public this week. It'll come with high expectations that will be hard to meet. Rather than buying the stock on its first day of trading, I'd do this instead.

According to recent reports, when SpaceX went public back in June, there was tremendous excitement around the IPO. The market was in much better shape than it is now. There weren't as many worries about rising interest rates. The mood was fairly positive. SpaceX initially soared in its first couple of days, at one point hitting a high of more than $225 -- well above its IPO price of $135.

Those early gains, however, would fizzle out. On Monday, it was back around its IPO price. While the business has been growing at a fast pace, with revenue totaling $14.6 billion during the three-month period ending Sept. 30, up from $5.6 billion a year ago, that kind of growth may already be priced in for a stock that's trading at such a high valuation.

NASDAQ · As of 3:36 PM ET 11/16/26.

Anthropic may face even worse challenges, as not only will expectations be high for the business, but it's going public at a time when investors are growing concerned about tech stocks as a whole. A decline looks to be inevitable for the stock because even if its valuation is lower than previously expected, I think it'll have a hard time proving to investors that it's worth even $1 trillion in market cap, let alone $1.4 trillion.

There are many risks associated with Anthropic that should give investors pause. There's significant competition in the tech sector, with many companies trying to develop the best and most advanced chatbot. While Anthropic's Claude appears to be a preferred option for many enterprise clients today, there's no guarantee it will remain so in the long term. The lack of a sustainable competitive advantage, combined with its high valuation and lack of true accounting profits, makes this a high-risk stock to own.

A sell-off may come swiftly for Anthropic's stock, and it's only after a sharp reduction in value that I'd consider buying it.

An injury-time penalty from returning hero Raul Jimenez ensured Wolves came away with a point in their Championship opener after Blackburn had produced a comeback.

Wolves led through Marshall Munetsi’s cool finish on 18 minutes only for Sean McLoughlin’s first Blackburn goal to draw the visitors level on 27 minutes with a well-timed run and header.

The visitors turned the game around on 48 minutes through Andri Gudjohnsen’s close-range strike only for substitute Jimenez to level the game three minutes into injury time from the spot after Ryan Alebiosu handled the ball in the box. Jimenez and his wife marked his return to Molineux by giving 5,000 fans black scarves emblazoned with the words ‘Si Senor’ - a nod to his song - and Jimenez did not disappoint as he rifled in his penalty.

Sources indicate that LATE DRAMA! 😱Raul Jimenez cooly converts from the penalty spot, deep into added time to save a point for Wolves 🔥 pic.twitter.com/5h2lMxcHNU.

According to recent reports, cesar Peixoto wants Wolves to play with their heads rather than their hearts after the home side rescued a late point in the first game of the Championship season following relegation. Wolves replaced Rob Edwards with Portuguese coach Peixoto during the summer and he felt his side’s loss of organisation allowed Blackburn to take control of the game.

Peixoto mentioned: “One point is not what we want, we want three points. We lost some organisation in the second half and played more with our hearts and not our heads and brains.

“We have to keep our mental stability during the 90 minutes because we’re better when we’re organised. We need to play our way with our identity. It’s a lesson for us to understand when we lose organisation it’s more difficult for us and more easy for the opposition.

“We’re working hard to bring more solutions [into the club] but we need to work hard with the players we have. It’s the first game, there’s a lot to work on and a lot to improve.”.

Recent findings suggest that tony Mowbray took charge of Blackburn in the league for the first time since returning to the club for a second stint in the dugout. Rovers recorded their lowest league finish since Mowbray’s first stint in charge of the club last term but the Blackburn boss is confident his side have enough to beat the drop and climb up the table this campaign.

Sources indicate that mowbray stated: “Ultimately, it feels like a defeat, it’s a bit disappointing and a bit frustrating. I just felt a lot of decisions were starting to swing their way. It’s harsh to take, I don’t think they deserved a second goal. We asked the players to be brave and we were collectively very strong.

Industry observers note that “Everybody has us relegated, probably on the back of finishing 20th last season and losing a couple of our better players and not spending much money, which is a good motivation for the team. We deserved to win the game, we indicated there’s enough quality to give teams problems and I hope there’s help on the way [in the transfer window].”.

The first chance of the season came the way of Blackburn as a cross-field pass found Alebiosu down the right, who floated a ball into the box only for an unmarked Oladipo Afolayan to head wide from eight-yards out.

However, Wolves scored the first goal of the new campaign when Fer Lopez played a defence-splitting through ball into the path of Munetsi, who coolly found the net with a first time effort from the edge of the penalty area.

"A vibrant Molineux rejoices!" 🎉Marshall Munetsi cooly slots home for Wolves to give them the lead on the opening night of the Championship season 🥶 pic.twitter.com/tVHdbNv3Hq.

Blackburn drew level through an unlikely source just nine minutes later as McLoughlin headed in his first-ever goal in English football in more than 150 games when he met Ryoya Morishita’s cross from the right at the near post.

The home side had chances to retake the lead before the break as Lopez curled a shot narrowly over the top from 20-yards while Kieran Trippier teed up Mateus Mane for a chance as the teenager found the top of the net from distance.

Blackburn turned the game on its head minutes after the break as Gudjohnsen turned home Afolayan’s deflected ball in from the right from close range to stun Molineux into silence.

"It's brilliantly worked by Blackburn Rovers!" 💥Andri Guðjohnsen finishes from close range to turn the game around and the visitors the lead 👏 pic.twitter.com/vkKQQezicK.

Peixoto introduced Jimenez from the bench on the hour mark but even the Mexican could not lift Wolves with Blackburn comfortable for long periods as frustration grew in the stands.

However, Alebiosu handled Jackson Tchatchoua’s cross from the left in injury time and the referee awarded a spot kick which allowed Jimenez to mark his Wolves return with an equaliser from 12-yards as he sent Balazs Toth the wrong way.

When Wolverhampton Wanderers last attacked the Championship under a Portuguese manager newly introduced to English football, it proved a vintage season.

Molineux was under the spell of Nuno Espírito Santo in that 2017-18 campaign, and the big question is whether César Peixoto can lead a repeat nearly a decade later.

Peixoto was a surprise appointment in June, replacing Rob Edwards, and he has been entrusted with the mission of returning Wolves to the Premier League at the first time of asking.

“I have changed some things with set-pieces and some things in other moments of the game because I want the team to be organised and understand all the different moments within a match. During pre-season we have scored some goals from high pressing, but we will not be able to press high in every moment of every game. The players have to understand the game and recognise what each moment requires. It is vital that we work as a team. When we can press high, we’ll press high. When we need to defend in a mid-block, we will stay organised. When the opposition pushes us deeper, which will sometimes happen, we have to be organised there as well.

“There are a lot of crosses in the Championship, for example, so the team needs to understand what to do in those situations. We want to play our football, be offensive and react strongly when we lose the ball, but we also need to understand the different moments of the game. I think we are at a good level to attack the Championship.”.

According to recent reports, the 2026/27 Championship season kicks off at Molineux as Wolves host Blackburn, with the home side hoping to put the bad memories of last season firmly behind them. There are newly introduced playoff rules in place for this season, with six places now up for grabs in the play-offs.

In a recent development, wolves are aiming to return to the Premier League at the first attempt, having endured a miserable season in the top flight last year as they finished bottom with just three wins to their name. It has been a summer of change at the club as they chose to change managers. Rob Edwards lost his job in what was a shock move and was replaced by 46-year-old Cesar Peixoto, with this being his first head coaching position outside of his home country Portugal. Back in 2017/18, Wolves won the Championship title led by Peixoto’s compatriot Nuno Espirito Santo.

In a recent development, “I am ready,” Peixoto told Wolves’ club website. “We have worked very hard during pre-season, and I think we have had a great pre-season. All the players have worked very, very hard and they understand what I want from them. I am ready and confident going into the first game. Football is football, whether it is in Portugal or England, but there are different characteristics to the game here. We have watched, observed and analysed the Championship. We did that work before I came to the club, so we know what to expect.

“It is going to be a tough season with good teams, but we are prepared to fight for the three points game after game and week after week. We know what we want from the team and we know what our big goal is. We’re going to work very hard and fight to achieve that goal.”.

According to recent reports, they have brought in vast experience on the player side in the shape of Kieran Trippier and Raul Jimenez, who is back at Molineux three years after leaving for Fulham. Although they have lost Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes to Aston Villa, most of their squad has stayed intact as they pursue promotion back to the top flight. It is a special year for the club as they celebrate their 150th anniversary.

In a recent development, blackburn, led by experienced manager Tony Mowbray, did not enjoy a great season in the Championship last year, finishing down in 20th place and just five points above the relegation zone. 14 years have now passed since Blackburn last played in the top flight.

“I think it is a tough start,” Mowbray noted. “On paper, I would suggest the first couple of games, particularly, jumped out as a tough start. One of the Premier League sides from last season, away from home. They have got a very talented squad, a pretty expensive squad. They have got some very good individual talent. Yet, there is an argument to say they have not won many football matches in the last calendar year. So, what we get, we will have to wait and see.”.

These sides last met in the FA Cup during the 2024/25 season, with Wolves winning that fourth-round tie 2-0 thanks to goals from Matheus Cunha and Gomes, both of whom are now plying their trade elsewhere. The omens would appear to be on Wolves’ side as they are unbeaten in their last eight league meetings with Blackburn. Both sides progressed to the second round of the League Cup last weekend, with Wolves beating Port Vale 3-0 and Blackburn overcoming Burton Albion 2-1.

#3649. Breaking: How To Combine External And Proprietary Data Without Losing Control

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1300 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: How To Combine External And Proprietary Data Without Losing Control

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1300 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, as access to some external data sources becomes more restricted, companies must find ways to gain valuable insights without exposing sensitive information or giving up control of their proprietary assets.
  • Industry observers note that these concerns make privacy and governance as important as the technology used to connect datasets.
  • It has been revealed that treat external data as a rented input with a return path.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, as access to some external data sources becomes more restricted, companies must find ways to gain valuable insights without exposing sensitive information or giving up control of their proprietary assets. Combining outside information with internal records can provide a fuller picture, but it also raises questions about who can access the data, what can be shared, and how the information will be used.

Industry observers note that these concerns make privacy and governance as important as the technology used to connect datasets. Here, members of Forbes Technology Council share strategies for combining external and proprietary data while maintaining privacy, security and organizational control.

It has been revealed that treat external data as a rented input with a return path. Pull it in only as narrow, purpose-built signals, and build in a way to send it back: a documented use, an expiry and a kill switch. Privacy and control break less frequently on the first join than on the third reuse, when nobody remembers what the data was cleared for. - Stefan Gogoll, andagon Holding GmbH.

Industry observers note that every platform starts with “move your data here.” Moving data is the most painful job in the business. Do not move the data to the intelligence. Move the intelligence to the data and extract the meaning. Send the question in, compute there and bring back the answer. The value was never in the rows. - Prafull Khare, Radiant Digital.

Sources indicate that forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

According to recent reports, data clean rooms and federated queries let teams match external signals against proprietary records without either side handing over raw data. Pair that with clear governance on who can query what and log every access. The result is richer insight, with sensitive information staying inside the organization’s own walls. - Yardley Pohl, interos.ai.

Clean rooms and federated queries protect data in transit, but the real privacy risk sits in the join. Before combining outside data with yours, know which of your fields are personal, which keys link records, and how reliable those links are. A clean room can’t fix a bad join, so map your own data first, then decide what may be matched and by whom. - Frederik Riskær Pedersen, Maplith.

Companies should focus on open-source intelligence instead of acquiring massive, intrusive datasets. Companies can often go much further by making better use of publicly available information. Cross-referencing internal anomalies with publicly available threat signals can identify credible risks earlier so teams can act on them without resorting to deep surveillance or giving up control of their data. - Jonathan Graff, Liferaft.

Sources indicate that share what you learned, not what you have. Keep raw data behind your own firewall, let external data in only to inform your systems there, and give partners just the resulting insights, never the records themselves. Learning crosses the wall; data never does. That keeps both privacy and control intact. - Charles Yeomans, Atombeam.

Industry observers note that A customer data platform is a data orchestration layer that aggregates and unifies external and proprietary data in a single view. Data is pulled together only when needed and is written back to the original source so, regardless of location, all key information remains under your organizational governance, with privacy and control intact. - Martin Taylor, Content Guru.

In a recent development, in our banking work, customer data often cannot leave the client’s environment. So, we send the analysis to where the data sits and only the aggregated results come back. Each party keeps control of its own data. What makes it work is agreeing in advance on a short list of approved questions and who may ask them, so privacy is settled before anyone runs a query. - Dimitar Dimitrov, Accedia.

Recent findings suggest that one effective approach is to use federated learning, which enables companies to train AI models across decentralized data sources, both external and proprietary, without sharing or exposing raw data. This method lets organizations gain broader insights while keeping sensitive information secure on their own systems, preserving privacy and regulatory compliance. - Will Conaway, Tuxedo Cat Consulting.

It has been revealed that combine the data at the moment of execution, not before it. The instinct is to pool external and proprietary data in a governed space, then work on it. Change the timing instead. Fuse the two inside one governed execution step, scoped to that action, with every access logged and removed when the step ends. Nothing persists. The riskiest thing in most architectures isn’t the query; it’s the combined dataset left sitting afterward. Don’t create one. - Corey Ercanbrack, Vasion.

According to recent reports, there’s no single control; it depends on the business need. For one-way sharing, anonymize data and restrict access to what’s strictly needed. For two-way collaboration, tokenize identifiers so you can map results back to internal records while partners never see who or what is behind them. In both cases, clean rooms or shared workspaces add need-to-know access to anonymization and tokenization. - Kim Bozzella, Protiviti.

Build a synthetic twin of your proprietary data: an artificial version that preserves statistical patterns without exposing real customer records. Join it with external data, test it with partners, and train models on it. Before sharing, test that no synthetic record can be traced to a real person. Poor generation can still leak information, and rare edge cases may be missed, so validate findings on the real data internally. You keep control of the originals. - Gayathri Kolandaisami, Quantumzet Technologies.

In a recent development, rather than moving raw data between systems, combine it inside a governed corporate digital identity profile. For example, real-time data from authoritative public sources is retrieved on demand and combined with a bank’s private customer information. Every data point is sourced and timestamped, proprietary data stays in the bank’s control, and AI gets accurate, auditable data via permissioned access, supporting both innovation and regulatory review. - Alex Ford, Encompass Corporation.

It has been revealed that use private set intersection when the useful part of the data is the overlap. If a company wants to compare its customer list with an external dataset, for example, it can identify or calculate something about the records they have in common without handing over the rest of either dataset. That means you can get the signal you need without creating a fresh copy of everyone’s data somewhere else. - Elton Chan, Second Talent.

Industry observers note that I’d start with the decision the data is meant to improve. Once that is clear, companies can bring the external signals they actually need into a controlled environment and limit how much proprietary information is exposed. I’ve found that starting with the use case usually leads to a simpler, more responsible data system. - Deniz Gezgin, Eightpoint.

It has been revealed that build a one-way door into an air-gapped system. Outside data lands first in a separate holding area, where its source, license and quality are checked. Only then is it read into the air-gapped environment that holds the proprietary data, with no route back out. Shared clean rooms ask companies to trust a space they do not fully control. A one-way door asks them to trust nothing, and every insight stays inside. - Vivek Thomas, AISensum.

Sources indicate that companies should prevent external information from automatically replacing trusted proprietary records. Outside sources can enrich business decisions, but they may contain conflicting or inaccurate values. Companies should keep original internal records intact and require approval before accepting material changes. This approach allows companies to use external insights while retaining control over the accuracy and integrity of their own information. - Salice Thomas, Wipro Limited.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that nvidia (NVDA -4.56%) is set to report results after the bell on Tuesday, Nov.
  • Recent findings suggest that it's also the graphics processing unit maker's first report since Jensen Huang resigned as CEO on Nov.
  • Index investors have a stake in this one, too.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that nvidia (NVDA -4.56%) is set to report results after the bell on Tuesday, Nov. 17, for the three months ending Oct. 25 (its fiscal 2027 third quarter). That makes Wednesday, Nov. 18, the first session when the S&P 500 (^GSPC -2.06%) can react to the numbers.

Recent findings suggest that it's also the graphics processing unit maker's first report since Jensen Huang resigned as CEO on Nov. 11. Chief financial officer Colette Kress is interim CEO, and Nvidia noted its results would still come out on schedule.

Index investors have a stake in this one, too. Nvidia makes up around 6% of the S&P 500's value, one of the largest weights among tech companies in the index. And as of this writing, the index stands near 7,560. That puts it around 3% under the record it set when it closed at 7,818.93 on Oct. 6.

It has been revealed that I went back over Nvidia's last 12 reports to check what the index did the next day. It rose seven times and dropped five times. On average, the move came to almost nothing.

In a recent development, I got every report date from Nvidia's own earnings releases, starting with Nov. 21, 2023, and paired it with the S&P 500's daily closing levels from Yahoo Finance, which don't include dividends. As Nvidia reports after the bell, each move goes from the report day's close to the next session's close.

It has been revealed that the largest gain was on Feb. 22, 2024, after Nvidia's February 2024 report, when the index rose around 2.1%. That was its best day in over a year. The two worst days were almost tied, with losses of around 1.6% on both Feb. 27, 2025, and Nov. 20, 2025.

Recent findings suggest that the other nine moves were small. None topped 0.8% either way, and one of the five down days hardly counts. On Aug. 29, 2024, the index ended at 5,591.96, less than a quarter point below its close the day before.

Industry observers note that all told, the 12 days averaged a gain of around 0.02%. And the median gain was around 0.2%.

To check whether those days stood out, I compared them with every session over the same span, from the Nov. 21, 2023, close through Nov. 12, 2026. The index climbed on around 56% of those days, so seven of 12 (58%) is roughly the same rate.

The size of the moves is where the report days differ a bit. Up or down, the S&P 500 moved an average of around 0.65% a day in those three years. On the 12 days after Nvidia's reports, it moved about 0.76%. And three of the 12 saw a swing of more than 1.5%, occurring in only about 9% of sessions. This arguably fits with Nvidia's size, because a 10% move in Nvidia's shares alone could shift the index by roughly 0.6% before accounting for other chip and AI stocks that often trade alongside it.

Recent findings suggest that of course, 12 days is a small sample, and three big days could easily be chance. The three also split two to one in favor of losses.

Sources indicate that for an investor in an S&P 500 index fund like the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO -2.09%), the longer view is likely the more helpful one. The index closed Nov. 21, 2023, the day of the first report in this set, at around 4,538. By Nov. 12, 2026, it had risen around 67% to 7,592.

NYSEMKT · As of 3:39 PM ET 11/16/26.

Together, the 12 days after Nvidia's reports added about 0.2% of that. So nearly all of the gain came on the other 734 sessions, which didn't follow an Nvidia report.

The November reports don't show a pattern, either. The index climbed around 0.4% after the November 2023 report and about 0.5% after the November 2024 report, then lost around 1.6% after the November 2025 report.

Of course, a massive day on Nov. 18 wouldn't look unusual this month. In the 10 sessions through Nov. 12, the S&P 500 swung more than 1.5% four times, and Nov. 5's drop of more than 4% was bigger than any of the 12 days in this set.

But nothing in Nvidia's report history highlights which way the index is likely to go next. The Vanguard ETF trades around $693 as I write, about 3.5% under its 52-week high of $718.47. I'd feel comfortable buying shares of the fund in the week of the report, just as I would in any other week.

Tyson Foods, Inc. (TSN +8.25%) reported fiscal 2026 results that aligned with management's updated projections, characterized by market share gains in Prepared Foods and significant volume growth in the Chicken segment. Management indicated a strategic shift toward a commercially led and operations-enabled organization to address historical gaps in innovation success and customer relationship management. The manufacturer is implementing a "One Tyson" strategy to integrate its protein segments and provide unified category growth intends for large retail and foodservice partners. While management expects improved Beef segment performance and continued momentum in Prepared Foods for fiscal 2027, these benefits are projected to be tempered by tightening commodity spreads and rising input costs in the Pork and Chicken divisions.

Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Tyson Foods Fourth Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call. [Operator Instructions] Please note, this event is being recorded. I would now like to turn the conference over to Jon Kathol, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Jon Kathol: Good morning, and welcome to Tyson Foods Fourth Quarter and Fiscal Year 2026 Earnings Conference Call. On today's call, Jeff Schomburger, President and CEO; Curt Calaway, CFO; and Wes Morris, COO, will provide prepared remarks. Following the prepared remarks, we will have a Q&A session with all 3. We have also provided a supplemental presentation, which may be referenced on today's call and is available on Tyson's Investor Relations website and via the link in our webcast. During today's call, we will make forward-looking statements regarding our expectations for the future. These forward-looking statements are provided pursuant to the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995.

According to recent reports, forward-looking statements include all comments reflecting our expectations, assumptions or beliefs about future events or performance that do not relate solely to historical periods. These statements are subject to risks, uncertainties and assumptions, which may cause actual results to differ materially from our current projections. Please refer to our forward-looking statement disclaimers on Slide 2 as well as our SEC filings for additional information concerning risk factors. We assume no obligation to update any forward-looking statements. Fiscal 2026 was a 53-week year with the additional week falling in the fourth quarter. To give you a comparable view, all results and year-over-year comparisons we discuss today are on a 52-week adjusted basis, unless otherwise noted.

Segment results are presented at the segment operating income level and discussed on an adjusted basis. References to earnings per share, segment operating income, operating income and operating margin are on an adjusted basis, unless otherwise noted. For reconciliation of these non-GAAP measures to their corresponding GAAP measures, please refer to our earnings press release. Now I will turn the call over to Jeff.

Jeffrey Schomburger: Thank you, Jon, and good morning, everyone. And thanks to you all who spent time with me helping me get going here. Fiscal 2026 came in where we said it would in September, adjusted operating income of $1.98 billion, adjusted EPS of $3.44. The shape was a little different, a little better in Beef, a little lighter in Chicken. The firm had a strong year. Prepared Foods grew segment operating income 5.5% to $1.3 billion and gained market share. Chicken earned $1.9 billion in a year when industry prices fell. Wes and Curt will take you through the segments and the outlook.

In a recent development, I want to spend my time on what matters most to you, what Tyson can become and how we get there. I am really fired up about the opportunities in front of this great organization. My dad is 95 years old. My wife is 60 years old. My kids are 23 and 25. Besides me, what do they have in common? Their doctors and influencers are telling them, eat more protein. I've been in this industry over 40 years, many with Procter & Gamble. No one ever stated, "Do more laundry," or "Change more diapers." This place is exciting. Selling more laundry and diapers is hard. Selling more protein is fun.

Protein is the biggest opportunity in food, a $273 billion retail category, growing faster than overall food. 7 in 10 Americans say they are trying to eat more protein. Younger households spend more than 3x what their parents spend on protein each week. Consumers eat protein throughout the day with meals and snacking at home and away, and we serve all occasions. They want food that tastes great, is nutritious, affordable and convenient, more protein, bolder flavors, simpler ingredients, especially the younger consumers we are going after. Now some of you look at Tyson through the beef cycle, and I get it. But I'd ask you to look at us the way our customers do.

Their job is to win in protein, fresh, frozen, deli, prepared and on the menu. It's how a retailer wins the trip and how an operator builds a restaurant. Nobody is better positioned to help them because we can bring 3 things nobody else brings together. First, scale across 3 proteins, about $32 billion of fresh meats business in Beef, Pork and Chicken. Fresh meat is the foundation of the meat case and the menu, reliably supplying it at scale gives us an enviable position to partner with retailers and food service operators and most by every one of our segments.

That's what lets us bring them our brands and value-added products, initiative growth with them and make the products they sell under their own private brands. And it means we see demand across 3 proteins and every price tier before anyone else does. Second, brands and value-added at scale, about $22 billion in sales. They are our most profitable businesses. We have 3 billion-dollar retail brands: Tyson at about $4.5 billion, Jimmy Dean at about $3 billion, and Hillshire at about $2.5 billion. We also have promising substantial brands with room to grow, Ball Park, Wright Brand, State Fair and Aidells.

Recent findings suggest that and we have emerging high-attribute brands we're now putting real focus behind, Nature Raised Farms, Smart Chicken, and Buena Mesa. We compete in every price tier, value, mainstream and premium, with our brands and with the products we make for our customers. Premiumization is a huge focus because that's where consumers are going. We see high growth in premium chicken and high-attribute brands like Hillshire Reserve, Hillshire Snacking, Smart Chicken and Wright Brand. Nobody else in food plays in good, better and best across multiple proteins like we do. Third, best cost. And let me be precise because best cost does not mean cheap.

Sources indicate that best cost is the lowest cost to make the product consumers and customers prefer in every tier. If we remove costs by taking out what makes the product worth buying, we've lost. We won't do that. Our scale gives us whole-animal economics and plants that run efficiently. We're going after best cost with AI in our plants and supply chain and robotics and automation on the line. That's the culture of this company. Best cost is what will let us keep investing in our products and brands through the cycle when others pull back. How these 3 fit together? Best cost funds products and brands consumers prefer. Preferred products and brands build scale with our customers.

Scale with customers fills our plants and keeps us best cost. The more consistently we run that cycle, the harder it is to copy because nobody else has all 3 pieces of scale: proteins, brands and best cost. We have to execute with excellence. But we do have work to do. The assets are in place, but we have to bring the same rigor and discipline we have in our operations through our growth capabilities, R&D, innovation, brand building and customer joint business planning. We are staffing to win and strengthening these capabilities. Winning preference in every category on every brand and product we produce is the biggest growth opportunity ahead for our brands.

Our innovation success rate is not where it needs to be. We show up to our largest customers as 3 companies, not one. It will take 1 or 2 years to show fully in results, and I'd rather tell you that now. None of this needs a major overhaul. It needs talent and execution. Execution is the only strategy a consumer and customer ever see. The measure that matters most to me is return on invested capital. Best cost raises it, mix toward brands and value-added raises it, a network running efficiently raises it. Every business will be held to earning above its cost of capital. Higher returns means more cash.

Industry observers note that more cash means we invest in the business first and return more to you. We will continue to measure ourselves on our financial and operational KPIs, just as we always have. But we are amping up our focus on other metrics to ensure our strategy is working. These include market share growth, Tyson brand's leading category growth, the percentage of our flagship products that are preferred as well as volume growth and household penetration. I look forward to sharing our journey with you on these metrics as we progress. I've watched this organization from the boardroom for 10 years through the work to rebuild the balance sheet and the operating discipline.

I helped place the strong BU leaders and function leaders we have and are developing today. That foundation is why we can do this organically, and it's why I took the job. My goal is to be disciplined in execution quarter after quarter, year after year. With that, Wes will take you through the segments and the innovation behind them.

Wes Morris: Thank you, Jeff. Our most important goal is to make our products and brands consumer preferred, the choice people make over the competition. Our brands must earn that preference. Over the latest 52 weeks, our retail branded portfolio grew volume even as total food and beverage category declined, led by Jimmy Dean, Hillshire Farm, Wright Brand and Aidells in Prepared Foods, and Nature Raised Farms and Tyson brand in Chicken. Our operating rule is simple, consumer preferred and best cost. Every flagship product should be provably preferred in a blind taste test with packaging and communication that makes the difference easy to see. Innovation puts that standard into practice.

Our Jimmy Dean high-protein platform debuted in January has sold about $38 million at retail with strong repeat rates and Tyson Chicken Cups have crossed $28 million. Early repeat is encouraging, and there is room to build distribution with most of these debuts in roughly 1/4 to 1/2 of stores. We will measure innovation by whether consumers come back, not just by sell-in. I will now walk through each segment's fourth quarter and full year performance, what drove it and what we're doing on the things we control.

In a recent development, our job in operations is to deliver best cost, which means the lowest cost to create a product line that consumers love and to extract full value from every part of the animal. Prepared Foods had a strong fourth quarter and year. In Q4, sales were $2.6 billion, up 0.4% with volume down 0.3% as retail growth was offset by business we chose to exit. Segment operating income was $321 million, up $43 million from a year ago with a margin of 12.6%, up 170 basis points on commodity favorability and improved mix, partially offset by higher transportation costs. The one soft spot in the quarter is bacon, where category dollars declined.

For the full year, segment operating income was $1.33 billion, up $69 million or 5.5% with a margin of 12.9% on sales of $10.3 billion, inside our guidance range. Pricing improved, driven by favorable mix towards branded retail that more than offset the higher beef and pork trim costs, higher transportation costs and incremental investment behind our brands. Full year volume was up 0.1%. In Prepared Foods retail, we have gained unit and volume share in 45 of 52 weeks, including 0.6 points of volume share this year. However, we still under-index on shelf space and display relative to our share of sales. But we are making progress. Total distribution points in Prepared Foods grew 4.4% in the fourth quarter.

In a recent development, closing the gap fully will be a multiyear opportunity and part of our '27 playbook, alongside target media, innovation and quality. As commodity costs ease, that benefit takes time to flow through production and inventory, and we expect it to show up in fiscal '27. We continue to invest behind the brands because that is what protects our share momentum. Our earnings cadence in this business is also becoming more balanced, which makes results smoother and more predictable. Chicken had a fantastic year. In the fourth quarter we had sales of $4.5 billion, up 1.3% on volume growth of 2%. Segment operating income for the quarter was $389 million, a margin of 8.7%.

According to recent reports, although we aren't directly tied to these commodity markets, industry cutout values fell about 25% from a year ago with tenders, breast meat, wings under the most pressure and higher grain costs and feed costs, along with higher freight and storage costs, weighed on the quarter. Consumer caution around discretionary spending also made for a more challenging foodservice environment. For the full year, Chicken delivered segment operating income of $1.86 billion at a margin of 10.7%, just $33 million below last year on sales of $17.2 billion. Volume grew 2.1%, our eighth consecutive quarter of volume growth. Our controllable end-to-end performance and our operating cost savings offset nearly all those headwinds.

In a recent development, as we have remarked in the past, our model is unique because a large portion of our business is insulated from the commodity market through our value-added branded mix, strategic customer relationships. Through innovation and multi-tiered branding within value-added chicken, we cater to what each consumer needs and give our customers a full range to grow with. Distribution gains among our top 10 customers lifted net sales, leading to Tyson value-added retail chicken volume growth of 3.7%. In Beef, the cattle cycle remains the dominant factor. Fourth quarter sales were $4.9 billion, down 10.5% as volume fell 12.7% on tight cattle supplies. Segment operating income was a loss of $171 million compared with a loss of $52 million last year.

The quarter includes a noncash write-down of $80 million on live cattle inventory as cattle prices fell after we purchased the animals, partly offset by lower operating costs, including network optimization benefits. For the full year, the segment lost $654 million on sales of $21.3 billion. Volume fell 12.2% as fewer cattle were available, partially offset by heavier carcass weights. As we revealed in August, we are restructuring our beef network around 3 advantaged facilities located in the cattle belt of the Central United States, running at higher capacity utilization.

Last week, we unveiled our intent to establish a new long-term partnership with Allied Beef Company designed to strengthen the domestic cattle supply chain and support the future of beef production. The collaboration creates a direct relationship between Tyson Foods and American ranchers, creating a more economically sustainable model across the supply chain, while supporting rancher opportunities and long-term growth. In anticipation of the partnership, we are moving forward with intends to fully reopen the second production shift at our Amarillo, Texas, beef facility. We have already begun restoring select second shift operations and expect the shift to be fully operational by summer of '27.

We expect the actions we have taken in Beef, along with a focus on customer mix, revenue management and cost discipline and working to extract full value from every part of the animal to benefit us throughout 2027. The challenges in our Beef segment are a cattle cycle problem, not a broad deterioration in the business. There are early signs industry economics are improving. As cattle costs ease and wholesale prices hold, packer margins are moving up from deeply negative levels. Heifer retention is up about 3%, which will tighten supply near term before it helps. And the phased reopening in the Mexican border is a tailwind for fiscal 2027 and beyond, although the start has been relatively slow.

Sources indicate that in Pork, fourth quarter sales were $1.4 billion, up 2.4% on volume growth of 7%. Segment operating income was $16 million, a margin of 1.1% compared with $47 million last year. Increased hog availability expanded industry supply and product values, bellies in particular, fell faster than hog costs. The pork industry cutout was down about 20% year-over-year in September. For the full year, Pork delivered segment operating income of $228 million and a margin of 3.6% with volume growth of 4.4%. Lower pork prices pressured fourth quarter results and challenges remain. However, our integration with Prepared Foods allows us to direct raw materials to their highest value uses across the portfolio.

Prepared Foods uses a sizable portion of our pork production. So lower pork prices can benefit that business through lower raw material costs. Last quarter, we brought both segments under a single president to strengthen coordination and help maximize their combined value. International had a strong fourth quarter with sales of $619 million, up 6.1% and segment operating income of $49 million, a margin of 7.9%. For the full year, International delivered $180 million at a margin of 7.6%, ahead of plan. With that, I will turn it over to Curt.

Industry observers note that curt Calaway: Thanks, Wes. For the full year, adjusted sales were $55.4 billion, up 1.1%, excluding legal contingency accruals. Total organization adjusted operating income was $1.98 billion, a margin of 3.5%. Segment operating income was $2.9 billion compared to $3.3 billion last year as higher beef losses outweighed growth in Prepared Foods. Corporate expenses and amortization were $968 million, $49 million lower than last year, reflecting cost discipline. Adjusted earnings per share were $3.44 compared to $4.12 last year. Our approach to capital remains disciplined, deliberate and forward-looking: maintain our balance sheet strength and our investment-grade credit profile, invest in the highest return areas of the business and return cash to shareholders.

According to recent reports, operating cash flows were $2.4 billion and capital expenditures were $770 million, resulting in free cash flow of $1.7 billion, up nearly $490 million. We ended the year with $4.1 billion of liquidity and net debt-to-adjusted EBITDA of 2.1x. We also returned cash to shareholders, paying $704 million in dividends, and we accelerated our share repurchases. For the full year, that is $1.1 billion returned to our shareholders. Also, in the first quarter of fiscal '27, we repurchased an additional $93 million or 1.76 million shares.

Now to fiscal '27, a 52-week year. So comparisons to fiscal '26 are on a 52-week adjusted basis. We expect sales to be down 3.5% to 5.5%, primarily reflecting lower beef volume following our network restructuring and tight cattle supply.

For perspective, we expect sales growth in the combined Chicken and Prepared Foods segments of 3% to 4% in 2027. Market-driven headwinds, mainly in Chicken and Pork, could outweigh the controllable improvements we are making across the businesses. We anticipate corporate expenses and amortization of $1 billion, net interest expense of approximately $360 million and an adjusted tax rate of around 25%.

In a recent development, we expect capital expenditures of $1.1 billion to $1.4 billion and free cash flow of $800 million to $1.3 billion, with capital directed to the highest return growth areas and liquidity well above our minimum target of $1 billion. Now to our segment outlook. USDA projects fiscal '27 total U.S. production to be up slightly between 0% to 1%, with Beef down about 2%, Pork relatively flat and Chicken up 1%. In Prepared Foods, we expect segment operating income of $1.25 billion to $1.4 billion, with volume growth driven by share of shelf, innovation and incremental brand investments. In Chicken, we expect segment operating income of $1.3 billion to $1.6 billion, lower than fiscal 2026.

Sources indicate that industry supply growth and higher grain and input costs will pressure the market, partially offset by better operating cost savings and a richer value-added mix. Our value-added mix and strategic customer relationships cushion the pressure, but do not eliminate it. In Beef, we expect the segment operating loss of $300 million to $100 million of segment operating income profit. We expect a full year of network optimization benefits to remove network bottlenecks and grow case-ready and value-added partnerships, while better market spreads help even as cattle supplies tighten. In Pork, we expect $75 million to $175 million of segment operating income, which is lower as spreads stay compressed, partially offset by operating gains.

In International, we expect $125 million to $200 million of segment operating income. Overall, we expect fiscal '27 to reflect continued improvement in our Prepared Foods businesses, a meaningful improvement in Beef, offset by market pressure in Chicken and Pork. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Shares of Arm Holdings (ARM -7.83%) fell on Monday, down 7.9% as of 3:45 p.m. EDT.

Arm certainly wasn't alone, as pretty much the entire sector fell hard on the day due to several factors, all of which relate to uncertainty over the AI build-out and specifically the fate of Nvidia (NVDA -4.50%) within the AI ecosystem.

Arm's downturn today may have been particularly severe due to its close relationship with Nvidia as a licensor for Nvidia's CPUs.

NASDAQ · As of 3:42 PM ET 11/16/26.

Semiconductor stocks were down sharply today, with some, like Arm Holdings, down more than others. There are likely a few reasons driving this sell-off.

It has been revealed that first, a prominent semiconductor and AI research firm, SemiAnalysis, reportedly issued a forecast update to institutional clients over the weekend, downgrading its prior growth forecast for AI accelerators through 2030. These cuts were relatively significant, with cuts to accelerator revenue estimates of 19%, 28%, 41%, and 40% for 2027 through 2030, respectively, compared with prior expectations.

Sources indicate that it should be noted that even with these cuts, SemiAnalysis still forecasts growth every year through 2030, just not as much. Furthermore, the cuts seem to bring SemiAnalysis' estimates more in line with Wall Street analysts’. However, the devil is in the details: the bulk of the cuts to estimates appear to be due to Nvidia chip pricing, while competitive vendors were less affected.

Combined with the fact that Nvidia reports earnings tomorrow in what will likely be a hugely consequential report without former CEO Jensen Huang, investors are understandably de-risking by selling the entire chip ecosystem today.

It has been revealed that for Arm specifically, Nvidia licenses Arm's technology to produce its CPUs, the latest of which is named Vera. While CPUs weren't part of SemiAnalysis' report, which focused on accelerators and GPUs, the association with Nvidia could be affecting Arm more than other chip stocks today. Oh, and starting from a high-looking valuation of 77.5 times forward earnings, even after today's sell-off, likely didn't help.

To be sure, Arm has customers other than Nvidia. In fact, virtually all major hyperscaler cloud companies license Arm's architecture for their custom CPUs. Furthermore, Arm has its own AGI CPU coming, with initial sales forecast to begin at the end of next year.

That's all very promising; however, Arm's high valuation relative to some other semiconductor companies likely means there are better buys available, especially after the sector's major sell-off over the past two months.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that anthropic is expanding its business as it looks to unlock more growth opportunities. Recently, it confirmed multiple productivity tools, including Claude Sheets, which may provide users with an alternative to Microsoft (MSFT -1.13%)'s Office products, including Excel.

The tech stock has been trading lower on the news. However, here's why I wouldn't be concerned if I were a Microsoft shareholder.

In a recent development, I've worked in accounting for several companies, ranging from small to large, including government, private, and public organizations. Time and time again, I've seen the same trend: businesses relying on Microsoft's products for their ease of use and simplicity. Even with large enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, owners inevitably end up exporting data to an Excel spreadsheet because it's easier to analyze there and create reports.

Alphabet already has a competing product with its own office software, including Google Sheets. Many businesses, however, aren't eager to load their financial data into it simply because of the perceived risk of storing it online.

Meanwhile, at a time when there are growing concerns about artificial intelligence (AI) companies and how well they safeguard data, I don't see Anthropic's office software doing much better.

It has been revealed that it may be appealing for individual users or smaller companies, but there's a reason Microsoft has managed to grow its business so effectively over the years, even though there have been rival products for companies to choose from, and that's trust. Organizations trust Microsoft's software, and it's often the default option for many businesses, and it's not simply because there is a lack of alternatives.

NASDAQ · As of 3:37 PM ET 11/16/26.

I've used spreadsheets for decades and can admit that Google Sheets has come a long way in rivaling Microsoft Excel, but it still falls well short of the capabilities and needs of many businesses.

When combined with its broader suite of products, including Outlook and Word, the familiarity of these products and the value proposition that Microsoft's Office software offers to both individual consumers and enterprise customers will make it difficult for any company to take significant market share in this area of its business. Demand remains robust, with Microsoft 365’s paid commercial seats topping more than 450 million.

Microsoft has a strong competitive advantage in this area, and its strength in the corporate world is why I think it makes for an excellent long-term buy.

VIDA Global Inc. (VIDA -11.94%) reported its third quarter results as a public company, emphasizing a strategic transition from competing for IT software budgets to capturing a portion of the larger corporate labor and services budget. Management reported the completion of several foundational initiatives, including the transition of computer agents out of beta and the introduction of outcome-based billing models. The company stated that its model-agnostic framework allows it to leverage improvements in general-purpose AI models to enhance the reliability and capabilities of its specialized business agents. Strategic distribution remains a priority through new co-sell and resell partnerships intended to scale deployment capacity without proportional increases in internal headcount.

iQIYI, Inc. (IQ -17.30%) reported a return to non-GAAP operating profitability while managing a transition toward a decentralized, AI-driven content ecosystem. Management detailed a shift from a centralized long-form video platform to a social media model integrating premium dramas with creator-uploaded works. This strategy incorporates AI to reduce production costs and cycles across animations and short-form dramas. The company maintained leadership in domestic market share for long-form dramas and children's content while achieving its first quarterly lead in the short-form drama category.

#3626. Breaking: Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

📅 09 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1025 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

📅 09 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1025 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt.
  • In a recent development, high-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago.
  • The high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt. It isn't time to ditch high-yield bonds, but investors should pay attention to the warning signs.

In a recent development, high-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago. The increase reflects a jump in yields across the curve as investors bake in more inflation from high energy prices and other pressures, including concern about the deficit — hitting nearly $2 trillion in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30.

The high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Credit spreads are the difference in yield between the bonds and Treasurys of similar maturities. Wider spreads mean investors are demanding higher yields for holding corporate debt, viewing it as riskier.

Spreads are at 315 basis points in the overall high-yield market, higher than a year ago but still below levels in March when they reached 346 bps. One basis point equals one one-hundredth of a percent, or 0.01%.

Recent findings suggest that the high-yield market consists of bonds rated BB+ by S&P and Fitch and Ba1 and under by Moody's. The lowest-rated cohort, CCC and below, has seen the most movement with spreads climbing dramatically over the past year to roughly 1,250 bps.

Right now, the high-yield market is "flashing yellow" but is "far from red," noted Michael Arone, chief investment strategist at State Street Investment Management.

It makes sense that investors are demanding more compensation for taking on additional credit risk as borrowing costs rise, he remarked.

Yields are elevated across the board with the 10-year Treasury reaching its highest level since 2002 earlier in the week.

"The bigger question is whether this is simply a repricing of interest rate risk, or the beginning of a more fundamental reassessment of credit quality," Arone said.

He's in a wait-and-see mode since earnings are still growing, interest-coverage ratios remain good, and while default rates have ticked up some, he believes it is not concerning.

That said, the starting point in spreads is likely weighing on investors' psyche, since they are still low by historical standards.

"There's a small margin of error here, which I also think raises the anxiety level," Arone explained. "The compensation that investors are receiving for taking on this credit risk isn't overwhelming relative to history, and therefore subtle changes in credit spreads can be concerning.".

While there may be concerns about part of the lower-rated market, the overall high-yield market is in good fundamental shape.

In fact, credit quality is at a record high, with BB bonds making up over 60% of the market compared with 38% prior to the global financial crisis, remarked Kelley Gerrity, a fixed income strategist at Morgan Stanley Investment Management.

"We've had higher-quality companies coming in, and with higher rates now, you also have more discipline from companies that are more indebted ... just because of the higher cost of capital, so that actually is creating a bit of a healthier picture as well," she remarked.

Recent findings suggest that the lowest tier of high yield has always been more speculative, since the bonds have a higher default risk. Therefore, it's no surprise that they are the ones seeing the most widening in spreads, noted Collin Martin, head of fixed income research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research.

Recent findings suggest that the overall move in high-yield spreads have been "orderly," he said. "Are there cracks forming? I think the cracks are logical cracks with the lowest-rated bonds and it's too early to say that it's spreading to the broad credit market.".

In addition, fluctuations within the CCC-rated and lower spreads have been idiosyncratic, Gerrity added. Morgan Stanley recently broke down the spreads in the lowest cohort into two buckets: performing assets and non-performing assets, which are defined as spreads above 1,000 bps.

The non-performing spread to worst is 2,818 bps, while the performing bucket — the biggest piece of the CCC market — is 461 bps, she mentioned.

In a recent development, "It is isolated," she said. "I'm not necessarily sure that that will go away anytime soon, but it doesn't tell the story of overall concern and flashing caution for credit markets right now.".

For now, investors should remain selective within higher yield, Gerrity advised.

"We're looking for the best relative value opportunities, and we think that exists within that single-B cohort, and so we're leaning into that," she said.

Investors should be concerned if there is a steep widening in the broader high-yield market.

But there's scant evidence of stress in the BB cohort. Spreads in that group are at 194 bps, up from 179 bps a year ago — although the move hasn't been in a straight line.

In a recent development, "We're going to be focusing our attention on what are considered some stronger businesses," Martin mentioned. "If we start to see the markets demand higher spreads there also, that's what we'll be looking at to see if risks are really rising.".

According to recent reports, it's also important to understand that the Federal Reserve is raising rates in a strong economic environment, said R.J. Gallo, chief investment officer of global fixed income at Federated Hermes. The central bank is concerned about an inflation problem amid high fossil fuel prices due to the Iran war, while growth has been stronger than expected, he noted.

"With growth being good as the reason that the Fed is hiking, then you wouldn't expect high yield to blow out because growth means revenues stay up, means cash flow and profitability stays up," he explained.

High yield becomes a disaster when the economy is heading into a sharp economic downturn, Gallo said.

"That's when spreads really widen out," he stated. "But a recession is not the odds-on bet. Now, talk to me in six months if the Fed keeps hiking over and over, if oil prices stay high for longer, well, then maybe we will start to wonder.".

Breaking: Bessent calls for ‘dramatic shakeup’ at Nvidia, urges outside CEO

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (611 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday called for a "dramatic shakeup" at Nvidia after CEO Jensen Huang's resignation, questioning whether the chipmaker pursued illicit sales of its advanced artificial intelligence chips to boost earnings.
  • Bessent said Nvidia's board should look outside the firm for its next chief executive and suggested other executives should face scrutiny over the chip giant's compliance with U.S.
  • "I want to keep coming back to what was the culture at Nvidia, and were they pressing these seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings?" Bessent stated in an interview on Fox News.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday called for a "dramatic shakeup" at Nvidia after CEO Jensen Huang's resignation, questioning whether the chipmaker pursued illicit sales of its advanced artificial intelligence chips to boost earnings.

Bessent said Nvidia's board should look outside the firm for its next chief executive and suggested other executives should face scrutiny over the chip giant's compliance with U.S. export controls.

"I want to keep coming back to what was the culture at Nvidia, and were they pressing these seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings?" Bessent stated in an interview on Fox News.

The remarks come amid a growing feud between Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over the suspected diversion of advanced AI chips to China, even as the Treasury secretary continues to defend President Donald Trump's handling of the matter.

Both Bessent and Lutnick are expected to accompany Trump to China this week, Semafor reported Sunday, putting the two Cabinet secretaries alongside the president as he prepares to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the APEC summit.

A White House official told Reuters on Thursday that the president maintains "complete confidence" in Lutnick, despite mounting scrutiny of the secretary’s handling of the Nvidia matter.

Huang resigned Thursday following revelations about his relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, whom U.S. intelligence officials suspect of spying for China. Megaspeed is suspected of diverting Nvidia chips to China in violation of U.S. export controls.

Nvidia named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress interim CEO.

Bessent suggested Sunday that Nvidia's problems extended well beyond Huang.

"If this were a bank and they hadn't complied like this, the OCC would be in there right now, and a lot of the executives would be removed," Bessent said, referring to the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency.

Bessent also questioned Nvidia's financial disclosures, pointing to a surge in reported Singapore revenue as its China sales fell.

Nvidia stopped separately reporting Singapore revenue in November 2025, saying a upcoming methodology based on customers' headquarters rather than billing addresses better reflected the geographic distribution of its sales.

Bessent's remarks came two days after he told CNBC's "Squawk Box" that several federal agencies had supported adding Megaspeed to the government's export blacklist for months.

"But Commerce has the pen," Bessent stated.

It has been revealed that the public rebuke followed reporting by Axios that Bessent confronted Lutnick in the White House Situation Room over Commerce's failure to act against Megaspeed. Commerce denied that the confrontation took place.

It has been revealed that lutnick is also facing scrutiny over his family's financial ties to Nvidia. CNBC reported Friday that Cantor Fitzgerald, the Wall Street firm formerly run by Lutnick and now led by his sons, has helped arrange billions of dollars in financing for Nvidia's business partners.

Sources indicate that cantor mentioned Nvidia share holdings fell nearly 50% over six months as national security concerns surrounding Huang escalated. The positions were associated with client swap transactions, not proprietary investments, the investment bank said.

There is no evidence Lutnick shared sensitive information with his sons or that Cantor traded on such information.

Industry observers note that bessent on Sunday remarked Trump had drawn a firm line against sales of chips more advanced than Nvidia's H200 to China. Trump himself authorized H200 sales to approved Chinese customers in December —following months of lobbying by Huang — in an arrangement under which the U.S. government would receive a 25% cut.

Bessent's latest criticism comes two days before Nvidia is scheduled to report its first quarterly earnings since Huang's departure.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Megaspeed told CNBC Sunday that Alice Huang left the company in August 2025 and remarked it has launched an internal probe into media reports concerning its business and supply chain.

The Singapore-based cloud computing tech giant has faced heightened scrutiny since former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang noted he had been unfaithful to his wife following reports linking him to former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang.

Sources indicate that U.S. intelligence officials believe Alice Huang is a Chinese intelligence asset, according to The Upcoming York Times.

Industry observers note that jensen Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia on Nov. 12 amid fallout from reports about his extramarital relationships, one of which was reportedly a direct report.

Sources indicate that "Ms. Alice Huang officially left Megaspeed effective August 30, 2025 and currently has no role with the Organization," Megaspeed remarked in an emailed statement shared with CNBC. "Megaspeed does not comment on Ms. Huang's personal and private matters," it added.

Megaspeed describes itself as a "core business partner" of Nvidia's computing power cloud business in the region, allowing customers to rent computing power from Nvidia GPUs, or graphics processing units — specialized chips designed to do many calculations at the same time.

The organization, which has offices in Singapore and Indonesia, has previously faced media and government scrutiny over whether chips supplied through its business were redirected to customers in China.

Megaspeed remarked Sunday that media reports about its business, supply chain and global operations are not supported by verifiable evidence and it has retained external legal counsel to conduct a "thorough internal investigation.".

"Megaspeed designs and maintains its global operational and supply-chain control frameworks to comply with all applicable laws and regulatory regimes, including United States export control requirements and local jurisdiction rules in every market where we operate," it said.

The firm added that it will review the reporting and communicate further with stakeholders as appropriate.

— CNBC's Anniek Bao and Jenni Reid helped contribute to this report.

NATO member Estonia to close Russia border after attempted 'sabotage' of drone maker

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (498 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • NATO member Estonia notes it is preparing to close road border crossings with Russia from Dec.
  • Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna said on Sunday that Russia's military intelligence service GRU had ordered an arson attack against Estonian drone maker Threod Systems in the early hours of Saturday morning.
  • Authorities said the attempted attack did not cause significant damage and eight people were detained in connection with it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

NATO member Estonia notes it is preparing to close road border crossings with Russia from Dec. 1, as it blames Moscow for an attempted "sabotage" of one of its defense companies.

Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna said on Sunday that Russia's military intelligence service GRU had ordered an arson attack against Estonian drone maker Threod Systems in the early hours of Saturday morning.

Authorities said the attempted attack did not cause significant damage and eight people were detained in connection with it.

Estonia, which shares a 294-kilometer (183-mile) border with Russia, mentioned closing the crossings would help to reduce Moscow's ability to conduct hostile activities against it and mitigate risks related to sanctions circumvention.

Tallinn has frequently raised the alarm over sabotage attacks against NATO countries that have been supporting Ukraine since Russia released the full-scale invasion of its neighbor in February 2022.

"This weekend's attempted sabotage against an Estonian defence organization, attributed by our security authorities to Russia's GRU, is yet another reminder that Russia's hostile activities extend far beyond Ukraine," Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna stated Sunday via social media.

Recent findings suggest that "Estonia is preparing to close its road border crossings with Russia in response. Hostile actions must have consequences.".

Tsahkna said he had informed his Finnish, Lithuanian and Latvian counterparts of the decision.

Russia's foreign ministry said it would assess Estonia's aims to close its border crossings, adding that if these plans were to come into force, it would be seen as "yet another bout of aggressive and unbridled Russophobia," according to state news agency Tass.

It did not directly comment on the accusation that Moscow is responsible for the attack on Threod Systems.

It has been revealed that "Estonia is building walls. Many countries, as history reveals, have built walls that have brought no good to their creators," Kremlin spokesman ​Dmitry Peskov remarked Monday, according to comments reported by Russian state news outlet Ria Novosti.

Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal mentioned the attack was part of Russia's broader "hybrid war" against Europe.

"We will not be intimidated. Estonia is preparing for the possibility of closing its border with Russia to reduce the risks to our people and national security," Michal said Sunday via social media.

According to recent reports, the latest incident follows an arson attack in mid-August against Milrem Robotics, an Estonian defense company that supplies Ukraine with unmanned military vehicles. Estonian authorities later blamed Russia for the attack. Moscow denied the allegation.

European security officials and lawmakers have previously warned about Russia's hybrid warfare. In September, Danish intelligence officials said Russia could launch a "limited" military attack against a NATO member in the coming months, saying the Kremlin appears more willing to take risks after more than 4½ years of war against Ukraine.

The Danish Defence Intelligence Service, or DDIS, identified a "low but growing risk" that Russia could carry out isolated strikes with long-range weapons on infrastructure that is critical to the support of Ukraine.
