  • Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.
  • His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.

Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.

His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.

Fernandes did at least get an assist, taking the second-minute corner which was powerfully headed home by Harry Maguire to give United the lead.

Amorim’s Milan equalised after a defensive mix-up allowed Gonçalo Ramos to break into the area and square for Samuel Chukwueze to roll home.

United were awarded their penalty just before half-time after Koni De Winter tugged back Youri Tielemans, but Torriani guessed correctly to leave Fernandes frustrated.

United retook the lead after Patrick Dorgu pounced on a loose backpass from Filippo Terracciano, but Milan equalised again when Chukwueze’s wayward shot was poked in by Alphadjo Cissè at the far post.

Marcus Rashford, who was frozen out by Amorim and loaned out to Aston Villa and then Barcelona, came on as a substitute on the hour for his first United appearance since returning from Spain.

But Milan went ahead in the 68th minute when Chukwueze’s cross was headed home by Ramos, and three minutes later former Chelsea midfielder Ruben Loftus-Cheek raced through to hit the fourth and cap a performance that underlines United’s need for reinforcements before their season starts in earnest next Saturday, away at Hull City.

Manchester United (4-2-3-1) Lammens; Mazraoui (Dalot 61), Maguire, Heaven (Martinez 61), Shaw; Tielemans, Santos (Mainoo 61); Diallo (Lacey 61), Fernandes, Dorgu (Rashford 61); Cunha (Mbeumo 61). Subs Zirkzee, Yoro, J Fletcher, T Fletcher, Amass, Collyer, Mee (g), Heath (g), Gabriel. Booked Dorgu.

AC Milan (3-4-2-1) Torriani; Terracciano (Gila 60), Winter (Vladimirov 84), Pavlovic (Diawara 84); Chukwueze, Musah (Ricci 76), Jashari (Modric 60), Estupinan (Bartesaghi 61); Loftus-Cheek (Comotto 84), Cisse (Saelemaekers 60); Ramos (Camarda 75). Subs Pittarella (g), Bouyer (g). Booked Estupinan.

Goals Chukwueze (37), Cisse (57), Ramos (68), Loftus-Cheek (71).

Michael Carrick believes Manchester United can push for the Premier League title, but has underlined the urgent need for signings.

The United head coach has taken heart from his squad’s promising preparations for the new campaign and, speaking at their Co Kildare summer base, he explained why he was confident they could build on last season’s third-place finish.

It has been revealed that carrick has been thrilled to hear United’s players discussing what they might achieve and has dared supporters to dream that they can get closer to last year’s champions Arsenal. But he is also a realist and recognises he is not blessed with options.

So far United have added Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, a reserve goalkeeper, but their £83.3m spend is significantly less than what newly promoted clubs Ipswich Town (£109.4m) and Coventry City (£92.2m) have invested in their squads.

Amorim’s side have gone intercontinental this summer, travelling from Scotland to Indonesia, via Australia, before arriving in Poland for the last of their four pre-season games.

In a recent development, at his AC Milan unveiling, Amorim was asked about the learnings from his United tenure that he would take into his upcoming role. He stated: “The first thing is it’s hard to explain the mistakes because for that I would have to explain the context of the last adventure.

Sources indicate that “It’s hard to say to you every mistake. The only thing I can say is that I learned a lot and I made some mistakes.

“I didn’t have the opportunity, and I’m sorry for that, I didn’t have the opportunity to say something to the Manchester United fans at the moment and I’m really proud to be their coach for a year in that time.

“But now it’s a different history. There are a lot of things that I could do better in the last experience but sometimes it’s like that, you need to learn to find the right spot to reach a different level and that’s my thinking here.

“Everyone learns from their experience. I learned a lot, I did some mistakes I will try to change, there are some thing you will never change but I think I will be a better manager, that’s all.”.

Welcome to live coverage of Manchester United’s final pre-season match, against AC Milan in Wroclaw, Poland. Michael Carrick’s side will look to apply the finishing touches to a promising summer on the pitch, which has included victories over Rosenborg and Atlético Madrid, plus a draw against European champions Paris St-Germain. The team will fly back to Manchester with the massive ones, the ones they have always wanted – the Snapdragon Cup and the Boyle Sports Cup – in tow.

At the Tarczynski Stadium there will be a reunion with former manager Ruben Amorim, who was appointed AC Milan’s head coach in June, five months after being sacked by United. Following a frustrating season under Massimiliano Allegri in which Milan fell out of the Champions League spots on the final day, the Rossoneri stated Amorim would bring a “modern dominant tactical approach”. His methods failed to cut through at Old Trafford, though, during a tumultuous 14-month reign which finally ended after the Portuguese “blew up” during a heated meeting with director of football Jason Wilcox. At Milan, Amorim has persisted with the 3-4-2-1 formation that was doomed at United.

Carrick made clear this week that United must strengthen if they are to challenge for titles. So far the club have brought in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, but they are still in the market for a left-back and another midfielder. The future of Marcus Rashford has also been a topic of conversation among United fans. The forward has not played for his boyhood club since December 2024 but has joined up with his team-mates in Poland and it remains to be seen if he features in Carrick’s forward planning.

Sources indicate that kobbie Mainoo, who did not play a minute at this summer’s World Cup, and Lisandro Martínez have also joined up with the team this week and could be handed their first minutes of pre-season having been named in the matchday squad. For Milan, new signing Gonçalo Ramos – bought from PSG for £63m – will make his first appearance in the famous red and black.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dopo un periodo difficile all’inizio della carriera in Italia, il difensore dice di affrontare gli errori con più serenità.

Mario Gila, ex Lazio oggi al Milan, ha raccontato di essersi rivolto a uno psicologo dopo un periodo difficile vissuto all’inizio della carriera in Italia. Il difensore ne ha parlato nel podcast The Chamber, nell’ambito di un’iniziativa rossonera dedicata al benessere mentale.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Gila ha descritto le pressioni di un mestiere che, visto dall’esterno, può far apparire un calciatore di Serie A come una persona privilegiata e con pochi problemi personali. Nella sua esperienza, invece, il lavoro richiede un impegno mentale continuo, dentro e fuori dal campo.

«Un calciatore tende sempre ad avere la mente attiva. È una professione che comporta un grande dispendio di energie mentali», ha spiegato Gila. Per questo cerca occasioni in cui entrare in contatto con se stesso e ritrovare quel Mario che, a volte, sente di perdere a causa del lavoro.

Il difensore ritiene che la professione possa allontanare i giocatori da se stessi, anche per le situazioni da gestire fuori dal campo. Alimentazione, preparazione atletica e allenamenti scandiscono la vita quotidiana: da calciatori, ha osservato, si resta tali ventiquattr’ore su ventiquattro. Tutto va tenuto sotto controllo per arrivare al fine settimana nelle migliori condizioni.

Gila ha parlato anche del peso della ricerca della perfezione: «La perfezione ti sfinisce, è estenuante, e credo anche noiosa fino a un certo punto». Secondo lui, inseguirla può impedire di vedere fino in fondo l’essenza autentica di una persona. Per molto tempo ha adottato quell’atteggiamento; ora prova ad accettare maggiormente gli altri per come sono e a comprenderne il momento.

Industry observers note that ripensando all’inizio della carriera in Italia, Gila ha detto di avere attraversato una fase dura e di aver toccato il fondo. «Grazie a uno psicologo sono riuscito a superarlo», ha raccontato. Prima era molto severo con se stesso: non si concedeva di sbagliare e, quando accadeva, si giudicava negativamente.

Oggi considera l’errore parte del mestiere e un’occasione per migliorare e crescere. Dice di affrontarlo con più serenità e di riuscire a elaborarlo meglio, senza rinunciare a cercare una soluzione, tanto sul piano professionale quanto su quello privato. Guardare una situazione negativa da una prospettiva positiva, ha spiegato, cambia il modo in cui vive ciò che è accaduto: il rumore che accompagnava l’errore lascia spazio alla calma.

In a recent development, per Gila è normale commettere lo stesso sbaglio più di una volta. In quei momenti ritiene più utile trattarsi con gentilezza e capire che cosa sia successo, anziché lasciarsi trascinare dalla negatività. L’obiettivo, nelle sue parole, è cercare di sentirsi in pace.

#3577. What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (745 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (745 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the tech giant's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.
  • According to recent reports, huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the company.
  • In a recent development, nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the tech giant's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.

According to recent reports, huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the company. Chief financial officer Colette Kress has been named interim CEO as the company searches for a permanent chief executive.

In a recent development, nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand. That could all change.

"Although we expect the company to fulfill all of its previously announced commitments, we believe that going forward, it may be more difficult for the company to negotiate new multi-party investments among ecosystem partners at the same scale it has done up to this point," Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider said in a note Thursday.

The news of Huang's resignation comes after investors were already concerned about the massive amount of debt being taken on to fund AI infrastructure.

Tech bond yields have risen and spreads have widened on credit default swaps, most notably in lower-rated names. Credit default swaps are contracts in which investors pay for protection in case the borrower can't repay its debt. Wider spreads indicate investors view the bonds as riskier.

On Friday, the yield on Nvidia's 4.5% bond due in 2031 sat at 5.717%, nearly 5% higher week to date. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

Sources indicate that tech stocks slumped Friday with the Nasdaq 100 closing down 1.2% as markets continued to digest the Nvidia news. Yields on hyperscaler bonds ticked slightly higher on Friday, signaling the broader concern about AI debt lingers.

Sources indicate that it's the smaller AI companies that could ultimately see an impact if Nvidia makes any changes to its AI financing. The company had $36 billion in off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements, or backstops, for neoclouds, according to its last quarterly financial filing in July.

Neoclouds CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN are all in Nvidia's portfolio. Their shares were down sharply Thursday.

CoreWeave, which has become the poster child for AI debt fears, saw its bond yields retreat after its quarterly earnings on Tuesday eased investor concerns. The yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 was 14.79% on Friday after climbing to 16.7% last week. The spread on its five-year CDS also dropped more than 17% week to date, although it remained above 1,000 — which is generally considered a sign of distress.

It remains unclear how Nvidia's support for those companies may change, said CreditSights analyst Andy Li.

"We don't know what the ultimate strategy for Nvidia is going to be coming out the other side," he noted.

"However, I think directionally, just given the fact that Jensen was so crucial in selling the Nvidia story and being a very aggressive deal maker, it's likely that a lot of this creative deal-making and circular financing and equity and credit support is going to moderate," he added.

CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator told CNBC Wednesday, before Huang's departure, that Nvidia "is not one person.".

In a recent development, "There are thousands of people over there that interface with thousands of people at my company every day. They integrate on the technology. They integrate on the physical infrastructure. They integrate on the networking," he said in an interview with "Squawk on the Street." "They have been a great partner for us for years. They will continue to be a great partner for us.".

According to recent reports, bob Lang, founder and chief strategist at Explosive Options, doesn't see any big changes in terms of Nvidia's relevance or its ability to finance for now. As CFO, Kress was involved in the financing deals, and the search for a permanent CEO is going to take some time, he noted.

The real problem is just how much money the firm will want to lend for AI financing, rather than, say using its hundreds of billions in free cash flow for other purposes, like share buybacks, capex, or acquisitions.

"Massive companies like Nvidia and Meta, they're holding all the cards," he remarked. "When they decide that the game is over, that's it — it's going to be curtains for some of these smaller companies.".

— CNBC'S Kif Leswing and Isabel O'Brien contributed reporting.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

(See the video above for Frank's complete chart breakdown.).

In a recent development, is the Nasdaq-100's recent bounce a sign that the bottom is in? We're going to look at several charts to help answer that question.

In a recent development, first, let's remember how we got here. In September, the NDX broke out from a bullish cup-and-handle pattern, producing a 33,200-upside target. That breakout quickly failed, however, and gave way to a bearish pattern that broke down aggressively two weeks ago.

The decline brought the index relatively close to its 26,350 downside target before the current rebound began.

Zooming out, it's telling to see where the bounce originated. Three key forms of support converged in the 25,000-26,000 area:.

This confluence of support helped encourage buying after a roughly 15% decline.

For perspective, we also see what larger drawdowns of 20%, 30%, 40%, and 50% would look like … a lot worse.

It has been revealed that the following chart tracks NDX drawdowns from 52-week highs going back to just after the financial crisis. Only a handful of declines exceeded 20%, and three produced relatively quick reversals: late 2018, the Covid lows in 2020 and April 2025.

Historically, buying into declines of approximately 15%–25% has generally paid off, even when additional downside occurred first (yellow highlights).

The chart also highlights previous declines of 10%–16% in green, putting the current pullback into perspective.

Recent findings suggest that the major exception was 2022, when the NDX eventually declined nearly 36% over approximately 10 months ... a much worse outcome, which many investors are concerned could happen again now.

That raises the key question: Are we experiencing another routine correction, or the early stages of a larger bear market?

One important clue will be how far this bounce progresses.

Sources indicate that any rally that fails to reclaim the previous highs could establish a significant lower high. Additional lower highs would provide stronger evidence of a developing, longer downtrend.

We saw this in March 2022, when that first sharp rebound effort failed to reach the previous high before a much more severe decline followed.

The bottom line: The current bounce is encouraging, particularly given where it originated and knowing how well buying prior 10-20% drawdowns has paid off.

From here, it's all about the follow through. We don't need to see new highs right away, but any rally from here that's met with another wave of strong selling could reignite downside momentum.

#3572. A major NFT marketplace is shutting down—5 years after the boom, there's a lesson for investors

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (923 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

A major NFT marketplace is shutting down—5 years after the boom, there's a lesson for investors

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (923 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Although the digital collectibles, known as nonfungible tokens, had existed since 2014, they exploded in popularity in 2021 alongside the cryptocurrency boom, becoming status symbols for celebrities and wealthy collectors.
  • Weekly NFT trading volume across major blockchains surged from about $4.4 million in late 2020 to a peak of $3.2 billion in August 2021, according to CryptoSlam data published by The Block.
  • Sources indicate that today, much of that trading activity has disappeared.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Five years ago, NFTs seemed to be everywhere.

Although the digital collectibles, known as nonfungible tokens, had existed since 2014, they exploded in popularity in 2021 alongside the cryptocurrency boom, becoming status symbols for celebrities and wealthy collectors.

Weekly NFT trading volume across major blockchains surged from about $4.4 million in late 2020 to a peak of $3.2 billion in August 2021, according to CryptoSlam data published by The Block.

Sources indicate that today, much of that trading activity has disappeared. Weekly NFT trading volume has fallen more than 99% since August 2021, and several major NFT marketplaces have closed. On Thursday, Blur, once the largest marketplace for Ethereum-based NFTs, shut down its website.

At the height of the boom, Twitter co-founder Jack Dorsey sold an NFT of his first tweet for $2.9 million, while a digital artwork by an artist known as Beeple fetched $69.3 million at Christie's. Paris Hilton and Jimmy Fallon showed off their Bored Ape NFTs on "The Tonight Show," and even McDonald's released NFTs celebrating the return of its McRib sandwich.

Recent findings suggest that back then, some buyers believed NFTs represented the future of digital ownership, while others bet they could resell them at higher prices. But as enthusiasm faded, so did the demand that had driven the digital tokens' values higher.

The NFT boom and bust shows how promptly speculative investments can unravel when demand dries up. For investors, it's a cautionary tale about spotting the warning signs before buying into the next craze, financial experts tell CNBC Make It.

Part of the initial appeal of NFTs was the promise of a fresh way for artists and other creators to make money from their work. Using blockchain technology, NFTs allowed creators to sell digital collectibles with verifiable ownership records and potentially earn royalties on subsequent sales through smart contracts.

More broadly, NFTs were touted as part of the future of digital ownership, with the potential to transform how people bought, sold and traded digital assets.

But establishing ownership of a digital collectible was different from creating lasting demand for it, claims Evan Mills, a financial advisor at wealth management firm Scholar Advising.

"NFTs tried to manufacture that demand," he says. "Blockchain could establish who owns the token, but it couldn't guarantee that anyone would really value the ownership at the end of the day.".

In practice, many of the NFTs that attracted attention were relatively simple digital images, such as cartoon animals or promotional artwork featuring beer cans.

Traditional collectibles, such as paintings, antiques and baseball cards, have established histories and communities of collectors that can sustain demand, Mills says. NFTs, by comparison, became enormously popular in a relatively short period.

In a recent development, unlike many traditional collectibles, however, NFTs could be created in virtually unlimited quantities. While individual collections might contain a limited number of tokens, there was little stopping creators from launching new series. At the height of the boom in 2022, roughly 500 new NFT collections were being created every day, according to blockchain analytics firm IntoTheBlock.

The rapid rise in NFT prices helped fuel expectations that buyers would continue paying more for them. But as enthusiasm faded, so did the pool of potential buyers.

And unlike stocks or bonds, most NFTs didn't generate income, meaning buyers hoping to turn a profit generally depended on someone else being willing to pay more for them, claims Martin Mulyadi, the YHB Endowed Chair in Accounting at Shenandoah University.

"Most NFTs paid nothing, so the only way to make money was finding a next buyer at a higher price," he indicates. "When the buyers stopped coming, there was nothing holding up the price.".

For everyday investors, the NFT bust is a reminder that an asset's popularity doesn't necessarily make it a worthwhile investment.

Recent findings suggest that one common justification for buying risky investments like collectibles is that they make up only a small portion of an otherwise diversified portfolio. Financial advisors often recommend limiting speculative holdings to money an investor can afford to lose. But keeping an investment small doesn't necessarily make it worthwhile, Mulyadi states.

"While keeping a bet small limits the damage, it doesn't turn a weak asset into a good one," he says.

Mills argues that investors can also confuse speculation with diversification.

According to recent reports, "Diversification is not just owning more things," he states. "It's owning things that have different economic characteristics that change the risk and return of your overall portfolio.".

In a recent development, for collectibles, that means looking beyond an item's scarcity or popularity to whether there's an established market of buyers likely to value it over time. Even then, future demand can be difficult to predict.

There's also a difference between buying a collectible because you actually like it and buying it because you think someone else will pay more for it. For many NFT speculators, the appeal was likely less about owning what was essentially a JPEG than the prospect of reselling it for a profit.

Before buying a speculative asset, Mills recommends asking two questions: What is the economic reason it should generate a return, and what role does it play in the overall portfolio? If an investor can't answer those questions, he claims, the investment may not belong in the portfolio at all.

"A bad investment doesn't become a good investment just because you only own a little bit of it," Mills notes.

#3570. Breaking: A trading strategy to ride out the Nvidia uncertainty and generate income in the process

Breaking: A trading strategy to ride out the Nvidia uncertainty and generate income in the process

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (630 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, jensen Huang's abrupt resignation has sent shockwaves through the tech sector, dragging Nvidia's (NVDA) stock down roughly 30% since Oct.
  • However, for opportunistic investors, this panic has made the stock cheaper (obviously) while options have become significantly more expensive.
  • It has been revealed that buying good companies at a discount is investing 101, but the current market dynamics may do something else for those who use options.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, jensen Huang's abrupt resignation has sent shockwaves through the tech sector, dragging Nvidia's (NVDA) stock down roughly 30% since Oct. 6. The market despises uncertainty, and losing a visionary founder, particularly one without a well-telegraphed succession proposal, makes it worse.

However, for opportunistic investors, this panic has made the stock cheaper (obviously) while options have become significantly more expensive. Trading in the $160s, Nvidia's valuation has taken a substantial haircut, yet its underlying business fundamentals remain largely intact. While Huang was the architect of Nvidia's AI dominance, the organization's moat — superior GPUs, the CUDA software ecosystem, and networking expertise — does not walk out the door with him. The company's structural advantage in the global artificial intelligence rollout persists.

It has been revealed that buying good companies at a discount is investing 101, but the current market dynamics may do something else for those who use options. Huang's departure guarantees that Nvidia will be operating under a cloud of transition for the foreseeable future. Executing a permanent CEO search while navigating global regulatory scrutiny takes time. Consequently, Nvidia's implied volatility (IV)—the market's pricing of expected future price swings — has spiked to highs not seen since the tariff tantrum in the first half of 2025, and this elevated IV is highly likely to persist for several months as the leadership drama slowly unfolds.

Recent findings suggest that this prolonged period of high implied volatility can be a goldmine for option sellers, specifically those executing options overlays such as covered call strategies. When you buy NVDA shares at these depressed levels and simultaneously sell out-of-the-money call options against your position, the premiums you collect are directly tied to IV. Because fear and transition-related uncertainty have dramatically inflated these option prices, the income generated from selling covered calls is now significantly higher than usual.

This lowers the risk profile of holding the stock considerably over time. Consistently collecting these inflated premiums systematically lowers your overall cost basis in the underlying shares. If the stock trades sideways or recovers slowly during the CEO search, you are generating an outsized cash yield on a stagnant asset. If the stock experiences further downside turbulence, the heavy premium income acts as a substantial downside buffer, meaningfully reducing the strategy's overall risk over time.

By deploying a persistent covered call strategy, investors can leverage the exact fear driving the stock down to generate robust, risk-reducing income while maintaining exposure to the undeniable future of AI.

Industry News: Cantwell urges Lutnick to stop AI chip sales to China ahead of Xi meeting

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Maria Cantwell, the top Democrat on the Senate commerce committee, alleged in a letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on Sunday that the department under his leadership failed to prevent China from accessing the U.S.'s most advanced artificial intelligence chips.
  • According to recent reports, in the letter, Cantwell prodded Lutnick to enforce export controls and stop the flow of AI chips to companies barred from receiving the technology.
  • Her urging comes as Washington reels from revelations that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with an alleged Chinese spy named Alice Huang.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that sen. Maria Cantwell, the top Democrat on the Senate commerce committee, alleged in a letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on Sunday that the department under his leadership failed to prevent China from accessing the U.S.'s most advanced artificial intelligence chips.

According to recent reports, in the letter, Cantwell prodded Lutnick to enforce export controls and stop the flow of AI chips to companies barred from receiving the technology. She sent the missive ahead of a planned meeting this week between U.S. officials and Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation, in China.

Her urging comes as Washington reels from revelations that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with an alleged Chinese spy named Alice Huang. Nvidia is the leading U.S. company designing advanced AI chips.

Alice Huang was an executive at Singaporean technology tech giant Megaspeed that allegedly smuggled restricted chips to China.

Lutnick, meanwhile, has come under fire for stalling efforts to crack down on chip sales to China and for his close personal relationship with Jensen Huang, who was a vocal opponent of export controls.

"The Department of Commerce has resisted efforts to restrict companies flagged as national security threats, weakened safeguards, and left open pathways for the PRC to train advanced AI models using sensitive American technology," Cantwell wrote to Lutnick. "These failures to carry out the law help give away America's technology advantage in AI.".

The Commerce Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Monday.

Cantwell called on Lutnick to use his authority to enforce a 2018 law, known as the Export Control Reform Act, which gives the Commerce Department broad latitude to enforce export controls and protect sensitive American technology.

She also cites potential financial conflicts involving Lutnick's sons, who control Cantor Fitzgerald, which she stated held $1.2 billion in Nvidia stock at the time of his nomination. And she notes the Trump administration's 25% fee on certain Nvidia chips sold to China, which she said could create "a perverse financial incentive to approve exports of sensitive American technology.".

"America's national security and AI leadership cannot be compromised by family business interests or a policy that generates federal revenue from exporting technology critical to our competitive edge," Cantwell wrote.

According to recent reports, both Democratic and Republican members of Congress have ramped up pressure on Lutnick and other Commerce Department officials after a Nov. 9 Fresh York Times report alleging the department may have slow-walked an investigation into Megaspeed.

On Thursday, Senate banking committee Chair Tim Scott, R-S.C., summoned both Huang and Lutnick to testify before his committee in December.

Lutnick has agreed to appear before the panel, Kristen Eichamer, a Commerce Department spokesperson, said in a statement last week.

And Democrats, who will take control of both the House and Senate in January, have signaled they will investigate Jensen Huang and Commerce officials.

Sources indicate that on Wednesday, Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., the top Democrat on the Senate banking panel, and Sen. Chris Coons, D-Del., the top Democrat on the Senate Foreign Relations subpanel with jurisdiction over East Asia and the Pacific, sent a letter to Lutnick, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller instructing them to preserve all documents and communications related to Nvidia's exports of "advanced AI chips to China or to entities that may divert such chips to China.".

Recent findings suggest that the letter gives all three officials until Nov. 17 to confirm that preservation directives have been issued.

Trump says he's OK with Jensen Huang returning as Nvidia CEO, sees no national security risk

💡 Key Takeaways
  • President Donald Trump said he would be open to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang returning to the company he resigned from last week amid the fallout from an extramarital relationship he had with an alleged Chinese spy.
  • "I think he learned a significant lesson," Trump noted of Huang when asked by reporters on Monday whether he wants to see the organization co-founder reinstated as CEO.
  • Trump, speaking to reporters outside the White House before departing for a trip to Asia, downplayed national security concerns stemming from the affair with a former executive of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based technology company that U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

President Donald Trump said he would be open to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang returning to the company he resigned from last week amid the fallout from an extramarital relationship he had with an alleged Chinese spy.

"I think he learned a significant lesson," Trump noted of Huang when asked by reporters on Monday whether he wants to see the organization co-founder reinstated as CEO.

Trump, speaking to reporters outside the White House before departing for a trip to Asia, downplayed national security concerns stemming from the affair with a former executive of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based technology company that U.S. officials suspect of having funneled Nvidia's advanced chips to China.

Sources indicate that "It was not put at risk, and our country is now stronger than ever before," Trump told reporters when asked about U.S. national security concerns. Trump is due to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum.

The president told reporters he is not planning to replace Howard Lutnick as commerce secretary after questions arose about the Cabinet member's handling of export controls involving Nvidia's advanced chips.

Republican and Democratic members of Congress have raised concerns about the national security implications of the episode after it was revealed that Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in the 1990s, had an extramarital affair with Chinese businesswoman and alleged spy Alice Huang. Nvidia is the leading global supplier of advanced artificial intelligence chips.

Critics argue the affair could jeopardize the U.S.' global dominance in AI and that it raises questions about influence exerted by Nvidia's Huang on regulators and lawmakers as he opposed export controls that limited the sale of the firm's chips to Chinese firms.

According to recent reports, the New York Times reported Tuesday that the U.S. believed Alice Huang was a Chinese spy and that Secretary of State Marco Rubio alerted Trump to the situation aboard Air Force One in May before Jensen Huang joined the president on a flight to China.

The Washington Post reported Friday that Rubio had issued a memo to Trump warning the president about Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy.

But Trump on Monday said "I haven't heard that" when asked about Rubio's warning.

It has been revealed that "I don't know that she is a spy. Usually, what happens with that is that any woman coming to the country that's a beautiful woman that comes from China, they say she's a spy," Trump said, of Alice Huang. "I don't know that she was a spy at all.".

Trump also attempted to defuse tension bubbling within his Cabinet between Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Lutnick.

Axios reported last week that Lutnick has "repeatedly stood in the way" of cracking down on companies suspected of diverting Nvidia's advanced AI chips to China, prompting a Situation Room confrontation between the men. Both are traveling with Trump on Monday to Asia, as is Rubio.

And Bessent, in an appearance on CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Friday, seemed to express frustration at Lutnick for not putting Megaspeed, Alice Huang's former company, on a Commerce Department list of companies that pose national security concerns.

Recent findings suggest that the departments of Treasury, Defense and State and the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative all "were in favor of putting Megaspeed on the 'entity list' for months," Bessent stated.

Trump acknowledged on Monday that Lutnick might have delayed putting Megaspeed on the list but defended his rationale as essential for diplomacy.

"He was doing that because you could have — if you didn't delay it, If you didn't do something — you could have a blow-up with China," Trump noted. "We're having a very good relationship with China right now, and I understand both sides of it, and I'll make a decision. But I understand very well both sides.".

Trump, who previously had stated he did not strategy to raise the Jensen Huang issue with Xi when they meet this week, said he may do so. He also said he may meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in China.

As Trump downplays concerns about fallout from the affair and advanced chips finding their way to China, Capitol Hill leaders are taking a different approach.

A spokesperson for House Foreign Affairs Committee Chair Brian Mast, R-Fla., told CNBC "negotiations are still going" about Jensen Huang testifying before a trio of House committees.

Mast, along with House Select China Committee Chair John Moolenaar, R-Mich., and House Intelligence Committee Chair Rick Crawford, R-Ark., had given Huang a deadline of 8 p.m. ET Friday to respond to their request to appear before the committees. Mast has said he would subpoena the former CEO if he doesn't accept the invitation voluntarily.

Nvidia fallout: Commerce targets loophole for China's data center use

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (855 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Commerce Department on Monday moved to close a loophole that has let Chinese companies lease Nvidia's advanced computing power from data centers in third countries, effectively circumventing controls on sensitive chip technology being exported to China.
  • The interim final rule from Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security is the first U.S.
  • The rule was "written by and at the direction of" the Treasury Department and the White House National Security Council, BIS said in a press release.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Commerce Department on Monday moved to close a loophole that has let Chinese companies lease Nvidia's advanced computing power from data centers in third countries, effectively circumventing controls on sensitive chip technology being exported to China.

The interim final rule from Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security is the first U.S. policy response to the scandal that led Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to resign last week after reports that he had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy who worked for Megaspeed, one of Nvidia's biggest Asian customers.

The rule was "written by and at the direction of" the Treasury Department and the White House National Security Council, BIS said in a press release.

The rule came after growing criticism of Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick for not doing enough to prevent possible diversion of Nvidia's most advanced chips to China in violation of American export controls.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, in an interview on Friday with CNBC's "Squawk Box," blamed the Commerce Department for not putting Singapore-based Megaspeed on its "entity list," which would restrict certain exports to it.

Share prices of Nvidia and other companies linked to the artificial intelligence trade fell Monday morning after the interim rule was confirmed, among them chipmakers Micron Technology, Intel and Advanced Micro Devices.

The rule is designed "to prevent certain foreign actors from leveraging advanced computing power based on U.S. technology to threaten U.S. national security and foreign policy interests," according to the text of the rule.

The new restrictions "will undermine the ability of companies headquartered in countries of concern from using" advanced artificial intelligence semiconductors produced by U.S. companies to train advanced AI models, the rule claims.

The rule also notes that a license will now "be required to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil (and any additional country designated by the Secretary of Commerce, in consultation with the Secretary of State or the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs) – countries which present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion.".

The New York Times reported on Nov. 9 that American authorities began investigating Singapore-based Megaspeed and one of its executives, Alice Huang, in 2024, "after the tech giant started importing billions of dollars' worth of advanced Nvidia A.I. equipment into Malaysia.".

In a recent development, "Megaspeed had been planning and constructing data centers around Southeast Asia to serve Chinese clients, including Alibaba, the Chinese tech giant," The Times reported that day. "While that behavior is legal, U.S. officials were concerned that some of the Nvidia chips the company had bought were illegally routed into China.".

According to recent reports, jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO last week after reports that he had an affair with Alice Huang, and that she was a spy working for China. The two are not related. China's government has denied the claim that Alice Huang was a spy.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who, as national security advisor, leads the National Security Council, warned President Donald Trump last spring that Jensen Huang was in a close relationship with Alice Huang, The Times has reported.

Chris McGuire, a former deputy senior director for technology and national security at the National Security Council, in a post on X called the new rule "a major step forward to countering Chinese smuggling of and access to advanced AI chips.".

According to recent reports, "The work here is not done, as there are some critical loopholes that remain open and need to be closed in a follow-up rule (namely those related to activities inside the United States)," wrote McGuire, a senior fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations. "Commerce should move extremely rapidly to close these. But this is the first time in over 18 months that the administration is starting to take export controls seriously, and does represent a meaningful step forward.".

McGuire stated that the fact that the fresh rule was written by and at the direction of the Treasury Department and the NSC "is remarkable and unprecedented.".

"I have never seen a BIS rule that was not written by BIS," he wrote. "That implies that Commerce was dragged kicking and screaming over the finish line by the White House and Treasury, and instructed to publish this rule rather than the rumored weaker one that it preferred. Remarkable.".

Commerce's newly introduced rule was published a day after Sen. Maria Cantwell of Washington state, the ranking Democrat on the Committee on Commerce, Science and Transportation, in a letter to Lutnick said that Chinese companies such as Alibaba and ByteDance have "used overseas data centers equipped with advanced Nvidia chips to train advanced AI models.".

Industry observers note that "These companies are exploiting a loophole in U.S. export controls by using advanced American chips in foreign data centers even when those chips are restricted from the [People's Republic of China]," Cantwell wrote.

"Despite warnings from the Bureau of Industry and Security that certain arrangements may violate existing restrictions, the Department of Commerce failed to close this loophole, allowing PRC companies to advance their AI capabilities using sensitive American technology," she wrote.

    • Following the donations, the chairman emeritus of Berkshire still owns 182,140 Class A shares — roughly $162 billion.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Billionaire Warren Buffett donated Berkshire Hathaway shares worth about $5.5 billion to four philanthropic foundations, stepping up his annual charitable giving from the prior year.

    Buffett, 96, converted 6,150 Class A Berkshire shares into 9,225,000 Class B shares and gave 3,690,000 of those shares to The Susan Thompson Buffett Foundation, and 1,845,000 shares each to The Sherwood Foundation, The Howard G. Buffett Foundation and NoVo Foundation — the foundations run by his three children, Susie, Howard and Peter Buffett.

    Following the donations, the chairman emeritus of Berkshire still owns 182,140 Class A shares — roughly $162 billion.

    Sources indicate that "Last Thanksgiving I wrote that kindness is costless but also priceless. A year later, I would only add that it compounds, and at a better rate than anything Charlie and I ever bought," wrote Buffett, who was succeeded as chairman in September by his son Howard, in his annual Thanksgiving message.

    Recent findings suggest that the letter was much shorter than his message last Thanksgiving. Charlie Munger, former vice chairman of Berkshire, passed away in November 2023.

    Berkshire shares have been on a tear recently, up more than 19% since the start of the fourth quarter and ending last week with four consecutive record high closes. That compares with the S&P 500's decline of 1.2% so far for the fourth quarter. Berkshire has been seen as a safe haven as investors have worried about the artificial intelligence buildout, corporate drama and geopolitical risk.

    The shares are now outperforming the S&P 500 for the year by about 7.5 percentage points.

    In his letter, Buffett reiterated that all of his Berkshire shares eventually will be donated to the four foundations, with the goal being to increase the size of the grants each year.

    Buffett wrote that the gifts were a signal of his confidence not only in his three children, but also in Berkshire CEO Greg Abel:.

    In a recent development, "My children have given thoughtfully to worthy causes for decades, and I trust 100% both their abilities and their fidelity. ... You heard plenty from me in September about my confidence in Berkshire. That confidence is as strong as ever," he stated.

    Sources indicate that referring to Munger and himself, Buffett added, "Both of us received beyond measurement costless benefits from a few teachers such as Ben Graham, Joe Rosenfield and Tom Murphy. Because of this we not only prospered mightily but were able to pass along many of the benefits we received.".

    "Warren continues to share his wisdom with us all during this holiday season. His example reflects the kindness he encourages in all of us," stated CEO Abel of the letter.

    Buffett closes his message with this advice: "This Thanksgiving, thank one of those selfless people in your own life. Better yet, be a benefactor for someone else.".

    OpenAI inks agreements with four independent evaluators to boost organization's safety work

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (649 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • OpenAI on Monday confirmed it has signed agreements with four independent evaluators to help support the artificial intelligence company's safety work.
    • The evaluators, Apollo Research, METR, Transluce and Goodfire, will initially conduct distinct pilot assessments around model behavior and safeguards, OpenAI stated.
    • "We expect this first phase of assessments to lead to longer-term, consistent embedded engagements over time that can continuously provide third party safety signals and recommended improvements on our most load bearing safety claims and safety cases," OpenAI said in a blog post.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    OpenAI on Monday confirmed it has signed agreements with four independent evaluators to help support the artificial intelligence company's safety work.

    The evaluators, Apollo Research, METR, Transluce and Goodfire, will initially conduct distinct pilot assessments around model behavior and safeguards, OpenAI stated. The company will give the organizations "deep access" to its internal systems as part of the agreements, adding that it plans to use what it learns to expand its work with independent experts going forward.

    "We expect this first phase of assessments to lead to longer-term, consistent embedded engagements over time that can continuously provide third party safety signals and recommended improvements on our most load bearing safety claims and safety cases," OpenAI said in a blog post.

    It has been revealed that independent evaluators have occupied a quiet corner of the multi-trillion-dollar AI industry thus far, but they've taken on outsized importance following a series of high-profile safety and security incidents this year. The nascent ecosystem is still ironing out best practices, including how its work should be funded and what the reporting structures should ultimately look like.

    Recent findings suggest that openAI CEO Sam Altman pledged to grant independent evaluators "employee-like access" to the organization in September, shortly after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said his company would do so as part of his call to slow down the pace of advanced model development. Anthropic has since declared agreements with evaluators including Accenture and METR, and it said in October that it's engaging in discussions with others.

    OpenAI's safety practices have been under intense scrutiny since July, when two of its models escaped containment, accessed the open internet and hacked a company called Hugging Face. Following the incident, OpenAI noted it would invest more in its safeguards and alignment work, which is the process by which the company works to ensure that its models act in accordance with human interests and values.

    The organization noted Monday that its pilot assessment with Apollo Research will explore whether its models covertly work against their developers' intentions, and whether its safeguards detect that behavior. Meanwhile, Goodfire will embed researchers within OpenAI to focus on training run monitoring, debugging and alignment, and METR intends to carry out two assessments focused on model alignment and monitoring.

    OpenAI stated Transluce will conduct an initial assessment of its post-training alignment evaluations, and that the organization prepares to conduct an eight-week-long follow-on assessment with broader access to additional models and information next year.

    The evaluators will get access to some of the "same internal resources" that OpenAI's own researchers use, including its source code, model checkpoints, training data and other documentation, according to the release. The organizations will also have access to relevant researchers and engineers within the company.

    OpenAI noted Apollo Research and Goodfire "accept financial compensation for their work," but that it is not contingent on the results of their evaluations. METR and Transluce do not accept compensation for their assessments, OpenAI said, but they might accept compute or API credits to help support their work.

    "We do not believe that accepting financial compensation prevents assessors from maintaining independence — but we believe it is vital to disclose this," OpenAI noted.

    The evaluators will be able to publish their findings, but OpenAI stated it reserves the right to redact confidential information.

    Sources indicate that disputes that arise between the firm and the third parties will be overseen by OpenAI's Safety Advisory Group, which is a group of senior officials from across the company that assesses model capabilities and safeguards, and other OpenAI executives. If disagreements are not resolved, they'll be escalated to the Safety and Security Committee, an independent oversight committee of the OpenAI Foundation's board.

    "We are committed to expanding this work and helping build the capacity and shared standards needed to sustain it," OpenAI said.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert?
    • It has been revealed that how about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it?
    • So what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert? No. While Ricardo Calafiori’s intervention was dramatic, it wasn’t that. Was it the seamless introduction of the latest signings, then? No, it wasn’t that either, despite the excellence of Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis.

    It has been revealed that how about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it? Again, the answer is no. Three unanswered goals against Manchester City will always grab a headline, but scorelines do not always define the nature of a performance or a team’s capabilities.

    So what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably? One word: hunger. The reason this was such an ominous afternoon for the chasing pack is the fact Mikel Arteta’s team played with intensity of a team with everything to prove.

    According to recent reports, title wins can sometimes sate ambition. Players don’t always want to climb the same mountain again, not least if reaching the peak was initially so draining, but everywhere you looked on a day when Cardiff was painted red and white was evidence that Arsenal remain ravenous for success.

    In a recent development, first Guimarães pounced out of the shadows to mug Jérémy Doku, leaving him in a heap. Then there was Gabriel Magalhães thundering into a befuddled Doku, celebrating in front of City’s fans as if he had scored, before Ben White flung himself in front of the Belgian, denying a clear-cut scoring opportunity.

    Ben White to the rescue with an incredible block 🦸📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZK0cNnFz5N.

    It has been revealed that another notable incident was Martin Odegaard, not long after he had glossed a fabulous display with a third goal, sprinting 30 yards to spook Gianluigi Donnarumma and make the Italian hurry his clearance. The victory was good, the trophy was nice, but the energy heartened Arteta more than anything.

    According to recent reports, “They are really good examples,” Arteta said. “The way the team tracks back is unbelievable, especially when, fitness-wise, we aren’t there yet. We had desire and composure on the ball. When you put your soul and your heart into every action, this is what happens. We want to do it again.

    According to recent reports, “The desire comes from them thinking: ‘I want to live that moment again. I want to have all the moments again and I want them to be even bigger.’ We know what it is going to take. We have never done it [retain the Premier League] at this football club. We know it will demand something special.”.

    Sources indicate that you could flip that and say it will take something special from the chasers. George Graham and Arsène Wenger could never hold on to the biggest prize during their reigns and you must return to Herbert Chapman, in Arsenal’s thriving 1930s, to find the only manager who went back-to-back.

    It can feel premature (and can be foolish) to go out on a limb before the first weekend, but there was just something about them that felt different. Often in the past they have been overtly tentative when playing City, but they came out of their corner this time swinging – and they landed.

    Enzo Maresca revealed afterwards that he “really didn’t like” how Arsenal had scored their first goal and that was putting it mildly, as there were 10 passes – broken only by the ball bouncing off Elliott Anderson’s shins – before Myles Lewis-Skelly ushered Calafiori into wreak havoc.

    You had to go back to 1968, when City played West Brom, to find the last first-minute goal – City’s Bobby Owen was the scorer that day – and how Calafiori enjoyed it, shaking his fist in delight as Arsenal’s noisy fans reminded everyone of their status.

    Riccardo Calafiori gives Arsenal the lead after just 24 seconds 🤯The assist from Myles Lewis-Skelly 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/aU0UsCB1Xs.

    Recent findings suggest that here was a rude awakening for Anderson, City’s upcoming £116m man. He was ever so slightly off the pace and that allowed Lewis-Skelly to slip a beautiful ball in behind the FA Cup winners’ defence and invite Calafiori to do the rest, which he did with assurance.

    Industry observers note that when Maresca watches back the video, he will see Abdukodir Khusanov sleeping and Phil Foden failing to press, but that should not detract from the quality of Arsenal’s interchanging – and it should also make whoever is hawking Lewis-Skelly around to clubs to think again. Why would he leave this?

    It should not have been the case that a goal so soon should have governed how the game progressed, but that is exactly what happened as Arsenal completely dominated. Whenever they lost possession, they recovered it as a matter of urgency. Without Pep Guardiola on the touchline, City were like Samson after Delilah shaved his hair, devoid of all power.

    Industry observers note that city, in contrast to their opponents, indicated a complete lack of desire and the second goal arrived when Odegaard was allowed time to flip a ball to the back post, where newly introduced boy Tzolis was arriving. The Greek headed back into the six-yard area and Kai Havertz did the rest.

    Kai Havertz finishes off a well-worked move to double Arsenal's lead 🤩📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tGkxCIBV8F.

    Arsenal were criticised – fairly – during their title-winning campaign for being too physical and relying on gamesmanship, but if Havertz and Odegaard can stay fit for a prolonged period, the difference in style will be like night and day.

    Throw in Tzolis, who was tricky and dynamic in Cardiff, to the mix and there will be another enhancement. He looks considerably better than Gabriel Martinelli, with more end product, and Bukayo Saka will do more down the right than Noni Madueke, who started here.

    Maresca knew, with his team lacking fitness, that it would be difficult to overhaul the deficit once they had gone two goals behind but, really, he was lucky that Arsenal did not administer a genuine hiding which, at one stage, seemed as though they might.

    Goal number three arrived just after the interval, again Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis were involved, combining to enable Odegaard to waltz into the area, hoodwinking Donnarumma so he sat down before sliding a contemptuous finish beyond him.

    Take a bow, Martin Ødegaard 😮‍💨Arsenal are flying against Man City!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/cMHbIyJ90D.

    Had they gone through the gears, there could have been more, but it didn’t matter. What Arsenal showed was far more significant than a couple of more goals when the game was being disrupted by substitutions. The tackles, the running, energy and commitment – that is what brought Arteta joy.

    “I’m extremely happy with the performance, the result and winning the first trophy,” Arteta purred.

    You would be brave to say it will be their last.

    According to recent reports, arsenal (4-2-3-1) Raya 7; White 7, Mosquera 7, Gabriel 7, Calafiori 7 (Hincapie h-t): Guimarães 7 (Rice h-t), Lewis-Skelly 8 (Zublimendi 75); Madueke 6 [Saka 60], Odegaard 8 (Eze 84), Tzolis 7; Havertz 7 (Gyokeres 75). Booked Calafiori, Odegaard. Subs Kepa (g), Merino, Dowman.

    Goals: Calafiori (1), Havertz (28), Odegaard (48).

    According to recent reports, manchester City (4-2-3-1) Donnarumma 5; Khusnaov 5, Dias 5, Gvardiol 5, O’Reilly 5; Anderson 5 (Lewis 60), Kovacic 5 (Gonzalez 79); Semenyo 6, Foden 5 (Cherki 60), Doku 6 (Grealish h-t); Haaland 5 (Marmoush 53). Booked Gvardiol, Foden. Subs Ait-Nouri, Reis, Nunes, Rulli (g).

    In a recent development, it’s really sad. I’ve been fighting with the Premier League to extend & accommodate more players in the squad. They deserve to be in the squad, so hopefully we can change that rule.

    Industry observers note that I think the goal we conceded after 25 seconds unfortunately affected the game in that moment. I think after the goal, the reaction was quite good before they scored the second one, we had three or four chances to score and draw the game but unfortunately we conceded the second one and it became more complicated.

    Sources indicate that A really, really good performance so early in the season. To play at the level we did and the desire we showed, I just told them that I really enjoyed watching them.

    He makes good decisions when a lot of people rush things, he did it twice in tight areas and two goals.

    I joined midway [in pre-season]. This is the third game since I have been back. The feeling has been good. Today is frustrating, and it is a final that we all wanted to win. If there is a lesson to be learnt in the final, let it be this one, as there’s a lot more coming. It is a positive energy.

    According to recent reports, the feeling of a lot of work to put into. It’s part of any transition for things to be not so perfect in the beginning. You need to push through, you need to communicate, and make things work between us. I feel we’re in a very good way, but we need to keep on working. There’s going to be lots of challenges along the way.

    Appears to the Community Shield trophy, which caught him a glancing blow to the face.

    Trophy lift gone wrong, featuring Declan Rice 😂🏆📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ghmGZJDxka.

    In a recent development, the players judge the correct level of celebration judiciously, but then Mikel Merino cracks and starts spraying the champagne. While it is a semi-competitive game, Arteta and his players will point out that they earned their place in the fixture by winning the league.

    Arsenal start the season with silverware 🏆The Community Shield belongs to the Gunners!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/M6GqsGkRF7.

    Recent findings suggest that what happens to them? I’m not sure the winners’ medals would take pride of place, let alone the silvers.

    Recent findings suggest that the league champions kick-off the domestic season with a resounding and stylish victory. Shades of 1998 and 2004 when they swept Manchester United aside in this fixture as title winners, only to fail to defend the crown in the season that followed. So maybe it is unwise to make bold forecasts, but it could not have gone better for Arteta. Odegaard, Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis caught the eye, and Arsenal had their usual solidarity defensively. City just completely off the pace, one to write off and move on.

    Recent findings suggest that marmoush is feeling his hip after a challenge by Mosquera. City have a free-kick wide right. Gabriel heads away Grealish’s delivery in trademark fashion.

    Sources indicate that just three minutes of added time to play. No City player is there to meet Cherki’s low cross and White can clear under little pressure.

    Sources indicate that rice uncharacteristically caught dallying in midfield but City cannot capitalise. Cheers from the Arsenal fans as Saka wins a throw in from Grealish. Marmoush with a chance to run at Mosquera, but his touch is far too heavy.

    City have a free-kick in a crossing position right of centre, but many of their fans are now packing up their banners and heading for the exits. If they haven’t already. Cherki’s delivery is poor, and Rice heads away.

    According to recent reports, city’s best move of the second half: Cherki gliding through the challenges and finding Semenyo with a lovely reverse pass, and his shot was drilled towards the far corner. Sharp reflexes by Raya to plunge to his right and save.

Whenever Arsenal have the ball in City’s half they look dangerous, whereas City’s possession has been sterile.

    Semenyo gave Hincapie a tough time in the League Cup final in March, and was not shy in boasting about it after the game. I suspect Hincapie is a defender who keeps a little black book of those who have crossed him.

    In a recent development, arsenal subs: Saka and Hincapue on for Calafiori and Madueke. Saka has braids this seasons, so a fresh look.

    Christos Tzolis registered 29 assists in 52 competitive games for Club Brugge last season. He’s on two assists in 48 competitive minutes for Arsenal.

    What composure from the Arsenal captain, running into the box untracked and sitting down first Gvardiol then Donnarumma before finding the empty net.     So far, Manchester City’s first glimpse of life after Pep Guardiola is inauspicious. Enzo Maresca might be his predecessor’s doppelgänger, but his attempt to emulate the same style has proved abortive: plenty of possession, but minimal impact. It smacks of desperation that Jack Grealish is being thrown in at half-time, his first appearance for the club for 15 months.

    It has been revealed that looks like a pre-planned change from Manchester City and Arsenal: Jack Grealish makes an unlikely comeback, replacing Doku, and Declan Rice replaces Bruno Guimaraes. Arsenal’s two big hitters in midfield sharing the game.

    “You’re getting sacked in the morning,” sing the Arsenal fans at Maresca as the whistle blows.

    There was a check for offside in the build up to Arsenal’s goal but the goal stands. Welcome back VAR, and consider the curtain raised on the new season. City enjoying some possession since conceding.

    That’s certainly one way to start a newly introduced season. It’s a fabulous team goal, with Lewis-Skelly at the heart of it. There has been a lot of talk about this teenager’s future but, in this reporter’s humble opinion, it should not even be a discussion. Losing a player of this quality, a product of the club’s academy, would be a terrible mistake.

There’s no space for Ethan Nwaneri, Gabriel Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus, Fabio Vieira or Reiss Nelson. All five of them could be sold by the end of the month.

It’s not only physical, it’s mental freshness. For the players not involved in the World Cup it is a bit different. They remain so competitive. They wanted to be involved and that’s good to see as well.

    Recent findings suggest that [On Bruno] He is a ball of energy. He has an unbelievable desire to win every ball. You sense he will drive the dressing room and when you bring someone with that competitive nature, it will only drive the boys.

    [On retaining the title] Still recognise the substantial margins that we have to improve as a team, individually and as well the ambition of the club which is unquestionable.

    It has been revealed that declan Rice and Bukayo Saka are with the group, but they have not kicked a ball in pre-season. They are looking at half hour of football at the absolute maximum today.

    In case any Arsenal fan had forgotten that last season ended with them losing a Champions League final on penalties, City fans are on hand to remind them. They have one European Cup to Arsenal’s zero. Away from the tin foil trophies, I’m sure much bottle-related mirth is on the cards, especially now broadcasters and fans are aware of the viral possibilities. Too aware, I would argue.

    Sources indicate that the pool of players who can improve the Premier League champions and Champions League finalists is a small one, but it is still fair to point out that Arsenal’s summer has not gone smoothly. They pursued Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior without success, and Arteta’s desire to take the team to a “different dimension” has so far gone unfulfilled., certainly in the forward positions.

    In a recent development, arsenal still look strong, but have they passed up a chance to pull away from the rest? Sam Wallace takes a look at their summer so far.

    Recent findings suggest that it would have been less stressful for Guardiola to go once he realised the great side of Kevin De Bruyne was nearing its end. Instead he opted to oversee a rebuild that gives his successor a greater chance of immediate success, going close to the title last season in what was effectively year one for a re-emerging City side. Guardiola must have known he was signing Gianluigi Donnarumma, Antoine Semenyo, Marc Guéhi and Rayan Cherki for someone else’s long-term benefit.

    The Community Shield returns to Cardiff’s Principality Stadium for the first time since 2006, and a different dynamic is at play between Arsenal and Manchester City.

    When the two clubs played at Wembley in this fixture three years ago, it felt like a more significant occasion for Arsenal as they sought to prove that the gap was closing to Pep Guardiola’s champions.

    Now it is Arsenal and Mikel Arteta who have a league title behind them, while Enzo Maresca is the manager hoping to build credibility as City turn the page post-Pep Guardiola.

    In truth, these two teams will look very different by the time the season gathers pace in autumn. World Cup exertions mean Elliot Anderson, Erling Haaland, Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka will be minimally involved in this game, while transfer looks remain up in the air for both camps.

    In a recent development, city appear bound to lose Rodri, in addition to Bernardo Silva and Tijjani Reijnders in central midfield. Rodri’s sale would expedite a move for Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi, and possibly Enzo Fernandez despite Chelsea’s insistence that the deadline to sign him for £120m has passed.

    Recent findings suggest that arsenal are also open for business, hoping to add a right-sided defender to help them cope with William Saliba’s absence. The £75m purchase of Bruno Guimarães means the champions’ midfield options look formidable, but so far it has been another summer without a level-raising forward signing. Christos Tzolis in and Leandro Trossard out looks canny business, but falls into the category of like for like.

    Although Arsenal held their nerve to see off City in the title race, they failed to win in three attempts against their rivals, including a limp defeat in the Carabao Cup final at Wembley. Arsenal also failed to win, or score, against Liverpool in the Premier League last season so their record in the massive games is an area for improvement.

    The victors this afternoon will claim to have laid a marker down, the losers will write the game off as a warm up exercise.

    Matteo Salvini ha scherzato su Lotito durante una visita al gazebo della Lega Giovani a Ponte Milvio, a Roma. Secondo quanto riportato da B-Lab Live!, Parlando di calcio con i ragazzi presenti, il leader della Lega ha salutato un tifoso biancoceleste con un «Forza Lazio» accompagnato da una battuta sui presidenti.

    CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

    Lo scambio è iniziato durante la foto di gruppo con il nuovo simbolo “Lega – Italia Federale”. Il vicepremier ha chiesto ai presenti di gridare «Forza Milan», tra le risate. Alcuni hanno risposto proponendo invece «Forza Roma».

    A quel punto il ministro dei Trasporti ha domandato se ci fosse «qualcuno per Lotito». Dopo i borbottii dei presenti, è stato Salvini a esclamare «Forza Lazio». Uno dei ragazzi si è avvicinato per dirgli di essere laziale: «Resisti ragazzo», gli ha risposto il leader della Lega, dandogli il cinque.
